content.article_text:
More than a year after his death, Ozzy Osbourne ‘s fans can relive his final performance through an upcoming concert film .

Sharon Osbourne recently shared her reaction to Ozzy & Black Sabbath : Back to the Beginning , premiering Oct. 25 in theaters, adding that her late husband would feel like “one lucky son of a bitch” after seeing the documentary from director Ben Wainwright-Pearce ( Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour , George Michael: The Faith Tour ).

“It was very hard to watch a lot of this film. I had to, but it was very, very hard,” Osbourne told Rolling Stone . “It’s bittersweet. It’s amazing. Everything about the show was amazing and just a joyous occasion and one that will go down in music history. I’m proud of that and that it was for my husband, and I’m so thankful to everyone that took part in it, for their time, their effort, their giving.”

Related Stories

Jack Osbourne Says Ozzy Movie Won’t Be “Artsy, Esoteric Biopic”: “Not What The Fans Want”

Noting that Ozzy “was in hospital for a week in England” before the July 5, 2025 concert, Sharon recalled his doctors “advised us not to do the show,” but he was determined.

Watch on Deadline

“They said it would kill him. We were all together and Ozzy said, ‘It’s not an option. It’s what I want,'” she revealed. “He said, ‘I know I’m dying. If I miss a few months of my life, I want to go this way. This is what I want.’ It was his wishes and we went through it. He said to me, ‘Another six months, what’s it going to do for me?'”

Ozzy died at age 76 weeks later on July 22, 2025, suffering a heart attack after living with coronary artery’s disease and Parkinson’s disease.

When asked what Ozzy would think of the concert film, Sharon surmised, “He would say, ‘How lucky am I?’ He goes, ‘I’m one lucky son of a bitch.’ And he knew it. He never took anything for granted, ever.”

The late Black Sabbath frontman’s family is also developing a biopic about him, five years after Sony Pictures and Polygram Entertainment were said to be in the works on a project.

content.article_text:
金沢21世紀美術館、長期休館を前にエルメスと特別プログラムを開催。「作品の継承」を問い直す

2027年5月から長期休館に入る 金沢21世紀美術館 が、 エルメス ジャポンと共同でワークショップとシンポジウムを開催する。現代美術作品を未来へどう受け継ぐのか、保存修復やものづくりの視点から考える。

金沢21世紀美術館 では、長期休館前の最後の展覧会「 今日から明日へ 作品を継承すること 」が10月31日から開幕する（2027年4月18日まで）。その関連プログラムとして、 エルメス ジャポンとともに、ワークショップとシンポジウム「壊れていくもの、継承していくもの」を11月に開催する予定だ。

展覧会「今日から明日へ 作品を継承すること」は、2004年の開館以来の歩みを振り返り、作品を未来へどう残していくのかという問いに向き合う。同館が収集してきた4000点超のコレクションのうち、保存・修復や展示方法の検討を要する作品を中心に取り上げる。コレクションには絵画や彫刻に加え、メディアアート、観客の参加や上演によって成立する作品なども含まれ、素材の経年変化や機材の旧式化、展示環境の変化など、その継承には多くの不確実性が伴う。こうした継承のあり方を考える上で一例となるのが、 宮永愛子 の《waiting for awakening -chair-》（2012）だ。素材のナフタリンが昇華し、次第に形を失っていくこの作品は、元の状態を保つことだけではないという作品の継承のあり方を考える。

本企画は、エルメスジャポンと金沢21世紀美術館が2024年から続けてきた協働を発展させたものだ。両者はこれまで、能登への支援や、アートを介した職人の技術と手仕事の継承に取り組んできた。こうした活動を踏まえ、今回は展覧会で掲げられた作品の修復と継承という問いを、アート、保存修復、ものづくりの視点から掘り下げる。

第1部のワークショップは、保存修復を手がかりに「作品を未来へ継承するために、何を残し、どのような変化を受け入れるのか」を考える内容だ。キュレーターズツアーとグループワークの2部構成で、専門知識の有無を問わず18歳以上であれば参加できる。11月1日または8日に同館で行われるキュレーターズツアーでは、保存修復の観点から展示作品を鑑賞し、継承について考えたい作品を参加者がそれぞれ選ぶ。続く11月13日には金沢美術工芸大学でグループワークを実施。参加者が持ち寄った考えをもとに、保存に困難が伴う作品や、現状を維持することを目的としていない作品が抱える課題について議論する。その後、各グループが1作品を選んで議論の内容を発表し、修復家で京都大学准教授の田口かおりがコメントを寄せる。

11月14日には、第2部のシンポジウムが金沢21世紀美術館で開催される。登壇するのは、修復家の田口かおり、彫刻の保存修復に携わりながら制作も行うアーティストの髙橋銑、インストーラーの有元利彦、アーティストの野村大輔、エルメスジャポン取締役会長の有賀昌男、金沢21世紀美術館館長の鷲田めるろの6人。ミクスト・メディアやメディアアート、インスタレーションなど、従来の保存修復の枠組みでは捉えきれない現代美術作品をどのように未来へ継承するのかについて議論する。モデレーターは同館学芸課長の角奈緒子が務める。なお、髙橋は本展のゲストアーティストとしても新作を発表する。さらにシンポジウムでは、エミール・エルメス・コレクションとスカーフのものづくりを通して、エルメスが受け継いできた修復と継承の思想が紹介される。

「壊れていくもの、継承していくもの」

content.title_original: 自宅前から「ラムセス大王」の巨大像が出土。住民が見つけた石材が思わぬ発見へ
content.article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "エジプト のベーベイト・エル・ハガル村で、 ラムセス2世 を表したとみられる巨大な彫像2体の一部が発見された。 Heritage Daily によると、地元住民が自宅前の土地で作業中に碑文の刻まれた石材を見つけ、通報したことが発掘のきっかけとなった。", "links": [{"text": "エジプト", "url": "https://artnewsjapan.com/tag/egypt"}, {"text": "ラムセス2世", "url": "https://artnewsjapan.com/tag/ramses2"}, {"text": "Heritage Daily", "url": "https://www.heritagedaily.com/2026/10/archaeologists-uncover-colossal-statues-of-ramses-ii-in-egypt/159585#google_vignette"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "調査にあたったのは、エジプト考古最高評議会（Supreme Council of Antiquities、以下SCA）の調査団だ。SCA事務総長のヒシャム・エル・レイシーによると、最初に見つかったのは、高さ約1.6メートルの巨大な石像の頭部。上エジプトと下エジプトの統一を象徴する、 古代エジプト の王の二重冠をかぶっていた。", "links": [{"text": "古代エジプト", "url": "https://artnewsjapan.com/tag/ancient_egypt"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "近くでは、像の背面を支える柱の一部も発見された。そこには、ラムセス2世の5つの王名の1つであるホルス名「ホル・カー・ナクト・メリー・マアト」が刻まれており、同王の像であることが判明した。この名は「強き雄牛、マアトに愛されし者」を意味する。マアトは、真理や正義、秩序をつかさどる女神だ。頭部の寸法から、調査団は像の本来の高さを、台座を含めて約8.5メートルと推定している。その規模は、ラムセス2世の治世に進められた建築・美術事業の壮大さを物語っている。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2体目は、古代エジプトの王に特徴的な縞模様の頭巾を着用している頭部と胴体部分だ。脚と台座は失われているが、残存部分の高さは約2.4メートルに達する。顔立ちが1体目と似ていることから、調査団はこちらもラムセス2世の像である可能性があるとみている。ただし、現段階では確定していない。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "調査団はさらに、2体目の像から約1メートル北で、長さ約1.3メートルのピンク色の花崗岩の石材を発見した。表面にはヒエログリフの碑文が一部残っており、ラムセス2世の王名に伴う称号「ネスウ・ビティ（Nesu-Bity、上下エジプト王）」と「サー・ラー（Sa-Ra、ラーの子）」が確認された。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「ラムセス大王」として知られるラムセス2世は、古代エジプト第19王朝の第3代の王で、紀元前1279年頃から紀元前1213年頃まで在位した。エジプトが帝国として最後の繁栄期を迎えた時代を治め、66年間に及ぶ治世の間に軍事遠征や大規模な建設事業を進め、数々の壮大な神殿や彫像を残した。高い人気と長い治世に加え、自らの権威を広める政治的な宣伝にも巧みだったことから、その名や姿を刻んだ碑文や美術作品がエジプト各地に残されている。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "SCAによると、調査団は引き続き碑文や彫像の造形的特徴、出土状況を調べ、像が当初置かれていた場所や役割、花崗岩の石材や周囲の遺構との関係を探っている。さらに、この地域のより古い時代の居住や建設活動を示す建築部材の発見も目指すという。（翻訳：編集部）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "from ARTnews", "links": [{"text": "ARTnews", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/monumental-statues-of-ramses-ii-discovered-egypt-1234802393/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2025年11月、世界の注目を浴びてついにグランドオープンした大エジプト博物館。そこには5000点を超えるツタンカーメン王の全財宝が史上初めて一堂に集められ、7000年にわたる古代エジプト文明の歴史が圧倒的物量と質で目の前に繰り広げられる。その数えきれない見どころの中から、3人の専門家が必見の展示を紹介する。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1. ラムセス2世像 大エジプト博物館の壮大なエントランスホールを見下ろしているのが、エジプト第19王朝3代目のファラオ、ラムセス2世の巨像だ。素材はピンク色の花崗岩で、高さ約11メートル、重さは82トンにも達する。 ラムセス2世はレバント地方（地中海東岸）への遠征を指揮した英傑で、世界最古の国家間平和条約を締結した王として知られる。1820年にミト・ラヒナ（古代エジプトの首都メンフィスがあった場所に位置する村）で発掘された巨大なラムセス2世像は、カイロ中心部の広場に約50年にわたって設置されていた。しかし、排ガスによる劣化が懸念されたため、エジプト政府は2006年に像をギザへ移動。その際の夜間運搬は大きな注目を浴びた。2018年1月には大エジプト博物館のアトリウムへ最後の移動を果たし、同館で最初に設置された主要展示物となった。 Photo: ©Grand Egyptian Museum"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2. クフ王の「太陽の船」 ギザの大ピラミッドを建造した第4王朝のファラオ、クフ王のために造られた「太陽の船」は、記録に残る世界最古の大型木造船の1つで、第1の船と第2の船の2隻が見つかっている。全長が40メートルを超える船にはレバノン杉が用いられ、紀元前2500年頃、クフ王のピラミッド南側の船坑に分解して封印された。2隻とも、太陽神ラーとともに王の魂が来世へ移動するためのものとされる。 4500年以上もの間、地下に隠されていた第1の船が見つかったのは1954年。エジプトの調査隊によって木片1224点が発掘され、修復の名手ハグ・アーメド・ユーセフ・ムスタファが十数年をかけて丹念に復元した。この船の構造は極めて精密で、理論上は今でもナイル川を航行できると言われている。なお、1987年には早稲田大学エジプト学研究所が、電磁波地中レーダー探査で第2の船の存在を確認。第1の船に隣接する坑から発掘され、現在は大エジプト博物館で復元作業が一般公開されている。 Photo: Ahmed Gomaa/Xinhua News Agency via Getty Images"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "3. ヘテプヘレス妃の副葬品 第4王朝のスネフェル王の妃で、クフ王の母にあたるヘテプヘレスの墓は、1925年にギザのピラミッド近くで発見された。この王朝は大ピラミッドやスフィンクスといった驚異的建造物で知られるが、ヘテプヘレスの墓からも当時の繁栄を偲ばせる副葬品の財宝が出土した。その1つが木と金銀で作られたヘッドレスト（枕）だ。古代エジプトにおいて枕は現世でも来世でも不可欠なもので、頭を支え、首を冷やし、さらには死者の復活を助けるとされていた。 ヘテプヘレスの墓から出土した遺物には、アラバスターの石棺（空の状態で見つかった）や寝台、椅子や輿、宝石箱などが含まれていた。しかし、その数年前に墓が発見されたツタンカーメンが世界的ブームとなっていたために、王妃のコレクションは当時ほとんど注目されなかった。その後、約1世紀を経て、ヘテプヘレスの財宝は古王国時代の眠りに関する儀礼を伝える貴重な記録として知られるようになっている。 Photo: Courtesy Ahmed Maatouk"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "4. ツタンカーメンの短剣 若くして王になったツタンカーメンの墓から出土した5000点以上の遺物の中で、長年にわたり研究者が魅了され、かつ頭を悩ませてきたのがこの短剣だ。ツタンカーメンの右太腿あたりで見つかった短剣は鉄でできているが、紀元前14世紀のエジプトにはまだ鉄の製錬法が伝わっていなかったからだ。 2016年、鉄にニッケルと微量のコバルトが混じった組成から、短剣に使われている金属は隕石由来のものだとする研究結果が発表された。この短剣を「天からの鉄」と呼んだ古代エジプト人は、おそらく隕石の貴重さを認識していたのだろう。専門家たちは、精巧な技法と希少な素材が用いられたツタンカーメンの短剣から、古代エジプトの生産技術の謎をさらに解明しようと研究を続けている。 Photo: Courtesy Ahmed Maatouk"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "5. ツタンカーメンの黄金の玉座 金箔で覆われ、ガラスや半貴石が象嵌されたツタンカーメンの玉座は、古代エジプトにおけるデザインのシンボル的存在だ。 1922年に王家の谷で発見された玉座は、エジプト王の絶大な地位と権威を物語っている。背もたれの板には椅子に座るツタンカーメンと、その肩に香油を塗ろうと手を伸ばす妻アンケセナーメンの姿が描かれ、神格化されたファラオの地位を示しつつも、王自身の優しく人間的な側面が表現されている。第18王朝後期にまでさかのぼるこの玉座は、少年王ツタンカーメンの象徴的な姿やファラオの不滅の神性を今に伝える重要な遺物だ。 Photo: Xin Mengchen/Xinhua News Agency via Getty Images"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "6. アンク・アフ・エン・コンスの碑（啓示の碑） エジプト末期王朝時代のものとされる彩色木版のステラ（碑）は、戦いの神モントゥの神官、アンク・アフ・エン・コンスのために作られた。描かれているのは、太陽神ラーと天空の神ホルスが融合したラー=ホルアクティ神に神官が供物を捧げる姿だ。 古王国時代に作られたこの彩色木像は、当時のビール作りの様子を捉えたものだ。2人の女性の召使いがもろみを濾して甕の中に麦汁を貯める姿からは、ビールが古代エジプトのさまざまな社会階層で欠かせない飲料だったことが窺える。 ビールは保存期間が短いことから、醸造作業は毎日の重要な仕事として生活に定着していた。カロリーや水分を補給するためだけでなく、日々の楽しみでもあったビールは、ピラミッド建設などの国家的事業に従事する労働者には、1日を通して決まった量が支給されたという。ニアンクペピケムの墓から副葬品として発見されたこの小像は、死後の世界でも楽しめるようにと、貴重なビールを墓に収めたことを示唆している。 Photo: Courtesy Ahmed Maatouk"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "12. 玉座に座るカフラー王 玉座に座り、前方を見つめている第4王朝のカフラー王は、王のための頭巾であるネメスを着け、ハヤブサの頭部を持つ天空の神ホルスに背後から頭部を守られている。玉座にあしらわれている蓮とパピルスの文様は、上エジプトと下エジプトの統一を象徴するものだ。像の素材には、サハラ砂漠の奥地でのみ採れる極めて硬い緑色の岩石、アノーサイト片麻岩が用いられている。 この像は、カフラーの「カー」（生命力）を宿すために作られた。古代エジプトの信仰では、カーには物理的な住処が必要とされ、ミイラが損傷した場合、カーの像がそれに代わる役割を果たすと考えられていた。 Photo: Courtesy Egyptian Museum of Cairo"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "13. テル・エル=ファルカで出土した小像 大きい像は高さ約60センチ、小さいほうは約30センチで、統治者とその後継者と考えられている。用いられている素材が物語るのは、ナイルデルタ地帯の交易ネットワークと富、そして像が支配階級の地位を示していることだ。 Photo: Courtesy Ahmed Maatouk"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "14. メンカウラー王の像 content.article_text:
エジプト のベーベイト・エル・ハガル村で、 ラムセス2世 を表したとみられる巨大な彫像2体の一部が発見された。 Heritage Daily によると、地元住民が自宅前の土地で作業中に碑文の刻まれた石材を見つけ、通報したことが発掘のきっかけとなった。

調査にあたったのは、エジプト考古最高評議会（Supreme Council of Antiquities、以下SCA）の調査団だ。SCA事務総長のヒシャム・エル・レイシーによると、最初に見つかったのは、高さ約1.6メートルの巨大な石像の頭部。上エジプトと下エジプトの統一を象徴する、 古代エジプト の王の二重冠をかぶっていた。

近くでは、像の背面を支える柱の一部も発見された。そこには、ラムセス2世の5つの王名の1つであるホルス名「ホル・カー・ナクト・メリー・マアト」が刻まれており、同王の像であることが判明した。この名は「強き雄牛、マアトに愛されし者」を意味する。マアトは、真理や正義、秩序をつかさどる女神だ。頭部の寸法から、調査団は像の本来の高さを、台座を含めて約8.5メートルと推定している。その規模は、ラムセス2世の治世に進められた建築・美術事業の壮大さを物語っている。

2体目は、古代エジプトの王に特徴的な縞模様の頭巾を着用している頭部と胴体部分だ。脚と台座は失われているが、残存部分の高さは約2.4メートルに達する。顔立ちが1体目と似ていることから、調査団はこちらもラムセス2世の像である可能性があるとみている。ただし、現段階では確定していない。

調査団はさらに、2体目の像から約1メートル北で、長さ約1.3メートルのピンク色の花崗岩の石材を発見した。表面にはヒエログリフの碑文が一部残っており、ラムセス2世の王名に伴う称号「ネスウ・ビティ（Nesu-Bity、上下エジプト王）」と「サー・ラー（Sa-Ra、ラーの子）」が確認された。

「ラムセス大王」として知られるラムセス2世は、古代エジプト第19王朝の第3代の王で、紀元前1279年頃から紀元前1213年頃まで在位した。エジプトが帝国として最後の繁栄期を迎えた時代を治め、66年間に及ぶ治世の間に軍事遠征や大規模な建設事業を進め、数々の壮大な神殿や彫像を残した。高い人気と長い治世に加え、自らの権威を広める政治的な宣伝にも巧みだったことから、その名や姿を刻んだ碑文や美術作品がエジプト各地に残されている。

SCAによると、調査団は引き続き碑文や彫像の造形的特徴、出土状況を調べ、像が当初置かれていた場所や役割、花崗岩の石材や周囲の遺構との関係を探っている。さらに、この地域のより古い時代の居住や建設活動を示す建築部材の発見も目指すという。（翻訳：編集部）

2025年11月、世界の注目を浴びてついにグランドオープンした大エジプト博物館。そこには5000点を超えるツタンカーメン王の全財宝が史上初めて一堂に集められ、7000年にわたる古代エジプト文明の歴史が圧倒的物量と質で目の前に繰り広げられる。その数えきれない見どころの中から、3人の専門家が必見の展示を紹介する。

1. ラムセス2世像 大エジプト博物館の壮大なエントランスホールを見下ろしているのが、エジプト第19王朝3代目のファラオ、ラムセス2世の巨像だ。素材はピンク色の花崗岩で、高さ約11メートル、重さは82トンにも達する。 ラムセス2世はレバント地方（地中海東岸）への遠征を指揮した英傑で、世界最古の国家間平和条約を締結した王として知られる。1820年にミト・ラヒナ（古代エジプトの首都メンフィスがあった場所に位置する村）で発掘された巨大なラムセス2世像は、カイロ中心部の広場に約50年にわたって設置されていた。しかし、排ガスによる劣化が懸念されたため、エジプト政府は2006年に像をギザへ移動。その際の夜間運搬は大きな注目を浴びた。2018年1月には大エジプト博物館のアトリウムへ最後の移動を果たし、同館で最初に設置された主要展示物となった。 Photo: ©Grand Egyptian Museum

2. クフ王の「太陽の船」 ギザの大ピラミッドを建造した第4王朝のファラオ、クフ王のために造られた「太陽の船」は、記録に残る世界最古の大型木造船の1つで、第1の船と第2の船の2隻が見つかっている。全長が40メートルを超える船にはレバノン杉が用いられ、紀元前2500年頃、クフ王のピラミッド南側の船坑に分解して封印された。2隻とも、太陽神ラーとともに王の魂が来世へ移動するためのものとされる。 4500年以上もの間、地下に隠されていた第1の船が見つかったのは1954年。エジプトの調査隊によって木片1224点が発掘され、修復の名手ハグ・アーメド・ユーセフ・ムスタファが十数年をかけて丹念に復元した。この船の構造は極めて精密で、理論上は今でもナイル川を航行できると言われている。なお、1987年には早稲田大学エジプト学研究所が、電磁波地中レーダー探査で第2の船の存在を確認。第1の船に隣接する坑から発掘され、現在は大エジプト博物館で復元作業が一般公開されている。 Photo: Ahmed Gomaa/Xinhua News Agency via Getty Images

3. ヘテプヘレス妃の副葬品 第4王朝のスネフェル王の妃で、クフ王の母にあたるヘテプヘレスの墓は、1925年にギザのピラミッド近くで発見された。この王朝は大ピラミッドやスフィンクスといった驚異的建造物で知られるが、ヘテプヘレスの墓からも当時の繁栄を偲ばせる副葬品の財宝が出土した。その1つが木と金銀で作られたヘッドレスト（枕）だ。古代エジプトにおいて枕は現世でも来世でも不可欠なもので、頭を支え、首を冷やし、さらには死者の復活を助けるとされていた。 ヘテプヘレスの墓から出土した遺物には、アラバスターの石棺（空の状態で見つかった）や寝台、椅子や輿、宝石箱などが含まれていた。しかし、その数年前に墓が発見されたツタンカーメンが世界的ブームとなっていたために、王妃のコレクションは当時ほとんど注目されなかった。その後、約1世紀を経て、ヘテプヘレスの財宝は古王国時代の眠りに関する儀礼を伝える貴重な記録として知られるようになっている。 Photo: Courtesy Ahmed Maatouk

4. ツタンカーメンの短剣 若くして王になったツタンカーメンの墓から出土した5000点以上の遺物の中で、長年にわたり研究者が魅了され、かつ頭を悩ませてきたのがこの短剣だ。ツタンカーメンの右太腿あたりで見つかった短剣は鉄でできているが、紀元前14世紀のエジプトにはまだ鉄の製錬法が伝わっていなかったからだ。 2016年、鉄にニッケルと微量のコバルトが混じった組成から、短剣に使われている金属は隕石由来のものだとする研究結果が発表された。この短剣を「天からの鉄」と呼んだ古代エジプト人は、おそらく隕石の貴重さを認識していたのだろう。専門家たちは、精巧な技法と希少な素材が用いられたツタンカーメンの短剣から、古代エジプトの生産技術の謎をさらに解明しようと研究を続けている。 Photo: Courtesy Ahmed Maatouk

5. ツタンカーメンの黄金の玉座 金箔で覆われ、ガラスや半貴石が象嵌されたツタンカーメンの玉座は、古代エジプトにおけるデザインのシンボル的存在だ。 1922年に王家の谷で発見された玉座は、エジプト王の絶大な地位と権威を物語っている。背もたれの板には椅子に座るツタンカーメンと、その肩に香油を塗ろうと手を伸ばす妻アンケセナーメンの姿が描かれ、神格化されたファラオの地位を示しつつも、王自身の優しく人間的な側面が表現されている。第18王朝後期にまでさかのぼるこの玉座は、少年王ツタンカーメンの象徴的な姿やファラオの不滅の神性を今に伝える重要な遺物だ。 Photo: Xin Mengchen/Xinhua News Agency via Getty Images

8. ウィッグスタンドとして使われた女性の頭部の彫刻 大きなイヤリングを付けた女性の頭部を模したこのウィッグスタンド（かつら台）は、かつらが文化やアイデンティティ表出のうえで大きな役割を担っていた当時の装いの習慣を今に伝えている。 かつらは社会階級や性別を超えて着用され、個人の身分や年齢、権威を示すものだった。たとえば、人毛のかつらは主にエリート階級が着用していたという。古代エジプトでは髪に関する埋葬習慣が重要視されていたことが知られているが、このウィッグスタンドは日常生活と自己表現におけるかつらの重要性を物語っている。 Photo: Curtis Ryan

9. Hekaemsaf（ヘカエムサフ）の黄金のマスク 古代エジプトにおけるマスクには、ミイラの頭部を保護するとともに神性を象徴する役割があり、死後の世界で魂が自らの身体を認識する助けになると考えられていた。この黄金の葬儀用マスクは、末期王朝時代の第26王朝でアマシス2世の船の監督官を務めたHekaemsaf（ヘカエムサフ）のものとされている。 マスクは槌を打って伸ばした金の板でできており、長石の目、黒曜石の瞳、ラピスラズリのまぶたと眉が、まるで生きているかのように感じさせる。これらの装飾は着用者の階級を表し、神の加護を象徴するものでもある。 Photo: Curtis Ryan

10. ラムセス2世の三連像 紀元前13世紀を中心に栄えた第19王朝時代に作られたこの赤御影石の彫刻は、ヘラクレオポリス・マグナ（現在のベニ・スエフ県に位置）のプタハ神殿で発見された。古代エジプトの都市メンフィスで信仰された創造神プタハと、プタハの妻で雌ライオンの頭を持つ戦争と治癒の女神セクメトを両脇に従えたラムセス2世の姿は、王が2体の神々に守られ、神々と協力関係にあることを視覚化し、その権威の高さを示している。 現在この像は大エジプト博物館の大階段に展示されており、ファラオが宇宙の秩序・均衡・調和の概念である「マアト」を支える役割を担っていたことを強く印象付けている。 Photo: Sayed Hassan/Getty Images

11. ビールを醸造する女性2人の小像 古王国時代に作られたこの彩色木像は、当時のビール作りの様子を捉えたものだ。2人の女性の召使いがもろみを濾して甕の中に麦汁を貯める姿からは、ビールが古代エジプトのさまざまな社会階層で欠かせない飲料だったことが窺える。 ビールは保存期間が短いことから、醸造作業は毎日の重要な仕事として生活に定着していた。カロリーや水分を補給するためだけでなく、日々の楽しみでもあったビールは、ピラミッド建設などの国家的事業に従事する労働者には、1日を通して決まった量が支給されたという。ニアンクペピケムの墓から副葬品として発見されたこの小像は、死後の世界でも楽しめるようにと、貴重なビールを墓に収めたことを示唆している。 Photo: Courtesy Ahmed Maatouk

12. 玉座に座るカフラー王 玉座に座り、前方を見つめている第4王朝のカフラー王は、王のための頭巾であるネメスを着け、ハヤブサの頭部を持つ天空の神ホルスに背後から頭部を守られている。玉座にあしらわれている蓮とパピルスの文様は、上エジプトと下エジプトの統一を象徴するものだ。像の素材には、サハラ砂漠の奥地でのみ採れる極めて硬い緑色の岩石、アノーサイト片麻岩が用いられている。 この像は、カフラーの「カー」（生命力）を宿すために作られた。古代エジプトの信仰では、カーには物理的な住処が必要とされ、ミイラが損傷した場合、カーの像がそれに代わる役割を果たすと考えられていた。 Photo: Courtesy Egyptian Museum of Cairo

13. テル・エル=ファルカで出土した小像 金で覆われたこの小像は、5000年以上前にさかのぼる先王朝時代、ナカダ文化ⅢB期（紀元前3350～紀元前2920年頃）のものと見られ、古代エジプト最古の統治者像とされる。像の芯部は木製で、ラピスラズリで縁取られた目が鋭い眼光を放っている。ラピスラズリは、現在のアフガニスタンに当たる産出地からはるばる輸入された貴重な素材だった。 大きい像は高さ約60センチ、小さいほうは約30センチで、統治者とその後継者と考えられている。用いられている素材が物語るのは、ナイルデルタ地帯の交易ネットワークと富、そして像が支配階級の地位を示していることだ。 Photo: Courtesy Ahmed Maatouk

14. メンカウラー王の像 第4王朝時代のこの像は、ギザのピラミッド群で最も小さいピラミッドを建造したファラオ、メンカウラー王を描いたものだ。当時理想とされた大きな手足や長い脚、力強く筋肉質な体が表現されている。 この像は、未完成に終わったメンカウラー谷の神殿に、他の像とともに安置される予定だったと考えられている。 Photo: Courtesy Mosaic Club

15. 金と銀でできたデンデラ神殿のホルス神像 この金と銀の像はハヤブサの姿をしたホルス神を表現したもので、頭上には太陽を表す金の円盤を戴いている。デンデラ神殿の宝物の1つとされ、盗賊から守るために司祭たちによって隠されていたと見られている。 デンデラ神殿の宝物とは、20世紀初頭にルクソールの北にあるデンデラ神殿とその周辺で発見された小像、宝飾品、儀式用器具、鏡などの遺物群だ。ホルス像は現在、同時に出土した他の遺物とともに展示されている。 Photo: Courtesy Vanilla Travels

A Fermata in Venice: Reconfiguring the Rhythms of the Everyday

In the Hong Kong Collateral Event “Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice” at the 61st Venice Biennale, Hong Kong artists Kingsley Ng and Angel Hui rediscover the quiet rhythms of the everyday through new site-specific installations.

Amongst the bustle of the Venice Biennale, the Hong Kong Collateral Event turns to a quieter register. Curated by the Hong Kong Museum of Art (HKMoA), Hong Kong’s first public art museum, the exhibition “Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice” marks the museum’s first curatorial undertaking for the Hong Kong exhibition at the Venice Biennale. Comprising five site-specific installations by artists Kingsley Ng and Angel Hui, the exhibition unfolds as a resonant journey rather than a series of isolated encounters, foregrounding the quotidian and the understated with a renewed attention.

Portrait of KINGSLEY NG (left) and his artwork Laundry Nocturne , 2026, and ANGEL HUI (right) and her artwork I Would Like to Open a Window for You , 2026. Courtesy Hong Kong Museum of Art.

The exhibition borrows fermata as its title and curatorial concept. In a musical score, it marks a moment of suspension, where a note or rest is prolonged at the performer’s discretion. In the Venetian cityscape, a fermata is a vaporetto stop—a threshold where passengers momentarily alight and embark. Resonating with the theme “In Minor Keys” of Venice Biennale 2026, the exhibition explores poetic rhythms in everyday life. Drawing on familiar yet fleeting moments in Hong Kong that subtly resemble those of Venice, the exhibition brings two cities into dialogue through shared conditions of everyday experience. Rooted in sensibilities shaped by Hong Kong, Ng and Hui bring distinct artistic approaches to a shared journey of self-discovery within the flow of life.

The fermata begins in the courtyard with Kingsley Ng. Ng is an established artist whose multimedia and spatial interventions often transform the familiar and the ethereal into meditative environments. Evolved from earlier renditions, his three installations for Venice trace his impressions between Venice and Hong Kong, attuning visitors to the overlooked rhythms of urban life. Sometimes, There Are Clouds in Puddles comprises mechanically triggered dichroic ribbons that reflect sunlight, creating the illusion of rain falling into five translucent, turquoise pools. Inspired by a poem by the late Hong Kong poet Leung Ping-kwan (Yasi), the work captures the fleeting magic of a rainy day.

This quiet observation continues indoors with Sky Well , where soap bubbles rotate within a hemispherical structure inspired by the spatial archetypes of wells in Hong Kong and Venice, as a single bulb sways above. The light is duplicated across the concave surface, creating an optical illusion that evokes an imagined cosmos and an image of impermanence.

KINGSLEY NG ,

Laundry Nocturne , 2026, dimensions variable. Courtesy Hong Kong Museum of Art.

Ng’s final installation, Laundry Nocturne , revisits the everyday ritual of drying laundry, a common sight across Hong Kong and Venice. A projected silhouette of a lone sheet sways under moonlight, accompanied by field recordings of Hong Kong’s night-time labour, from newspaper printing and sewage treatment to teahouses preparing for the day ahead. Gently bridging time zones, the sounds of nocturnal Hong Kong are carried into daytime Venice, as a tribute to the unseen labour. Across three installations, Ng reinterprets his impressions of Venice and observations of Hong Kong through humble materials, appreciating the everyday acts of maintenance that sustain urban life.

Alongside Ng’s immaterial approach, Angel Hui offers a tactile and sensory counterpoint through a practice grounded in material experimentation, daily objects and traditional artistic language. Known for her signature series of plastic bag embroidery, Hui, in her Venice debut, continues to transform the utilitarian into object for contemplation through traditional craftsmanship.

ANGEL HUI ,

I Would Like to Open a Window for You , 2026, dimensions variable. Courtesy Hong Kong Museum of Art.

Envisioned as one holistic spatial intervention, Hui’s two installations Drifting Sanctuary and I Would Like to Open a Window for You , span across two rooms as an imagined sanctuary, synchronised through light, sound and movement. In Drifting Sanctuary , plastic bags commonly used in Hong Kong to carry pet fish are stitched with goldfish motifs using traditional Suzhou embroidery technique, gently floating and flickering overhead. The shadows of the fish move across walls, drawing the gaze towards I Would Like to Open a Window for You , a slowly rotating wrought-iron window decorated with patterns characteristic to Hong Kong and Venice hand-crafted by Hui in collaboration with Hong Kong master artisans. The boundary between the two installations dissolves as the patterned silhouette of the window frame is cast across the rooms. Experienced as one immersive space, the two installations guide visitors towards Hui’s everyday observations in which overlooked objects hold care and delicate beauty.

The exhibition is neither a retreat nor a withdrawal from daily occurrences, but an invitation to linger with the familiar. Nestled in an old Venetian building opposite the main entrance of the Arsenale, “Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice” gives the uneventful everyday a moment to pause, remain and begin again.

Jointly presented by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department and the Hong Kong Arts Development Council (HKADC), and jointly organised by the Hong Kong Museum of Art (HKMoA) and the HKADC, the Hong Kong Collateral Event “Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice”, curated by the HKMoA, is currently on view in Venice (Campo della Tana, Castello 2126, 30122) through 22 November 2026.

content.editorial_excerpt_zh: 一场高速车祸令一名大学生终身与轮椅为伴，但这仅仅是《To Be Ordinary》故事的起点。这部敏感细腻、缓缓将人包裹其中的影片无意沿用残障题材的陈词滥调，转而铺陈出一幅开阔图景……

Ordinary》，影片稳健克制的形式与宽广的叙事格局，仍应能让它在影院中有不错的表现。该片作为唯一入选釜山电影节主竞赛单元的台湾作品完成首映后，将于本月晚些时候亮相东京国际电影节，并于11月中旬在台湾院线上映。影片很可能继续参加其他电影节，尤其是聚焦亚洲的单元；它足够通俗易懂，也足够动人，有望在全球范围内获得有限发行，不过专业流媒体平台或许才是最适合它的归宿。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Variety热门内容", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "李芸婵与《台北女子图鉴》编剧Ginger Wang共同撰写剧本，几乎没有浪费时间便让故事运转起来。影片开场是一段优美流畅的夜间跟拍镜头：22岁的Yu-jie（Junior Hsieh饰）骑着轻便摩托车，穿行于台北郊区被雨水打湿的道路上；Cicada配乐中宏大的弦乐营造出一种虚假的安宁。摄影指导Ming Lee的镜头此后肯定再也不会如此自由；这场遐想在一个路口戛然而止，Yu-jie被一辆汽车撞倒，驾车者是富有而年迈的马先生（Hsiu Shen Liang饰），他旋即陷入无法排解的愧疚。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Yu-jie在事故中幸存下来，却很快在医院得知自己再也无法行走。作为一名已经创办个人网页设计公司的大学生，他以惊人的克制接受了这个噩耗，迅速适应轮椅生活，并设法尽可能过上正常且充实的日子——其中也包括他与医院年轻物理治疗师Yi-Han（Phoebe Chu饰）逐渐萌芽的感情。", "translated": true}, {"type": Chen饰）正承受青春期早期的激素动荡，却觉得自己因这场悲剧而被冷落——她被迫照顾好自己，因为用母亲的话说，“家里已经够多事了”——于是开始以激烈的方式宣泄情绪。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": content.article_text:
A high-speed traffic accident leaves a college student in a wheelchair for life, but that’s merely the starting point of the narrative in “ To Be Ordinary ,” a sensitive, slowly enveloping film with scant interest in disability-drama cliché — instead offering an expansive portrait of how the young man’s entire family is affected by his accident over the course of more than a decade. Spanning marital strife, economic upheaval, coming-of-age pains and moral crisis, Taiwanese writer-director Lee Yun Chan ‘s fourth feature — her first since 2010’s “Dancing Without You” — has a lot of story to wrangle, but does so with a mostly delicate, empathetic touch, with a script that treats all individuals in this unhappy scenario with equal care and interest.

Related Stories

ESPN Launches ESPN JV YouTube Channel for Kids

Apple TV's Hit German Series 'Where’s Wanda?' Returns for Season 2, Again Asking: 'How Far Would You Go to Save Your Child?'

Since her last film, Lee has done mostly small-screen work — directing, among other things, the 2022 Disney+ series “Women in Taipei” — and if a certain televisual strain of melodrama occasional creeps into “To Be Ordinary,” the film’s sturdy formal restraint and expansive story scope should still serve it well in cinemas. Following its premiere as the only Taiwanese production in Busan’s main competition, the film will play at the Tokyo Film Festival later this month, opening theatrically in Taiwan in mid-November. Further festival play is likely, particularly in Asian-focused programs, and the film is accessible and moving enough for limited global distribution, though specialist streaming platforms may be its best bet.

Popular on Variety

Lee, who co-wrote the screenplay with “Women in Taipei” scribe Ginger Wang, wastes little time setting the story into motion, opening on a lovely, gliding nighttime tracking shot of 22-year-old Yu-jie (Junior Hsieh) on his moped, cruising the rain-slicked roads of suburban Taipei, as the grandiose strings of Cicada’s score conjure a false feeling of serenity. DP Ming Lee’s camera will certainly never be this free again; the reverie stops short when, at an intersection, Yu-jie is struck by a car, driven by the wealthy, elderly Mr Ma (Hsiu Shen Liang), who’s immediately beset with irremediable guilt.

Yu-jie survives the accident but soon learns, in hospital, that he’ll never walk again; a college student who has already started his own web design business, he accepts the bad news with remarkable stoicism, quickly adapting to life in a wheelchair and seeking ways to live the most normal, productive life possible — which includes a budding relationship with young hospital physiotherapist Yi-Han (Phoebe Chu).

If anything, the rest of his family has a harder time adjusting. His mother (Chang Shih Ying) and father (Weber Yang) were already at a fraught point in their marriage, and their son’s plight only drives them further apart, the situation exacerbated by Dad’s longtime unemployment. Meanwhile, Yu-jie’s younger sister Yu-ching (Pin Hsuan Chen), already facing the hormonal turmoil of early adolescence, feels sidelined by the tragedy — pressured to look after herself while, as her mother puts it, “there’s enough going on at home” — and begins to lash out.

At a pragmatic level, the family is aided by Mr Ma’s crushing conscience: In addition to the required legal settlement, he transfers ownership of his entire house to Yu-jie, and continues to contribute generously toward his medical bills and living expenses. But such generosity can itself become a burden of sorts to the benefactor, particularly as Mr Ma retreats into old age and ill health; avoiding drawing its characters along victims-and-villains lines, “To Be Ordinary” reserves compassion for all in this wretched turn of events, which gives it welcome dramatic complexity and maturity, particularly as the story spans 11 years of evolving consequences.

Thoughtful, closely-knit ensemble playing keeps the family dynamic believable even when the script takes a few convenient short cuts: Chen is especially affecting and volatile as a young woman growing up both as a kind of afterthought, and as a support system to her flailing parents. Lee directs proceedings with a handsome sobriety that befits the material, though between the persistently overcast visuals and the solemnly emotive writing, “To Be Ordinary” could stand an occasional injection of tonal surprise — an acknowledgement of the absurdity, hilarity or small domestic joys that sometimes disrupt hard times. Still, the film is never glib or unconsidered. There’s unassuming beauty in its even-handed, fair-minded worldview, and the space it gives its characters to reckon with sorrow, and find their own way out of it.

‘To Be Ordinary’ Review: A Compassionate, Even-Handed Taiwanese Family Melodrama

content.article_text:
Sylvester Stallone is opening up about how decades of daredevilry have affected him—and why he considers himself an “idiot” for continuing to do his own stunts year after year.

In a recent interview with Fox News Digital , the “Rocky” actor said he has “millions, millions of regrets” about his action career. “I could literally spend a half hour talking about injuries, the amount, not even like one, I’m talking about 30 hours, 30 minutes of just individual ones, because it becomes compounded. I have been injured many, many times, but after ‘Expendables,’ I ended up with nine back operations, three neck fusions. Both shoulders ripped out, eye, you know, all kinds of lens put … it’s been brutal,” he said, adding that he’s never been “quite the same” since the surgeries.

Related Stories

Why 'You Can See Everything' Could Make Oscars History as First Doc Nominated for Best Picture

Oscars: Cuba Selects 'Malecón' for International Feature Contest, Movistar Plus Acquires Spanish Streaming Rights (EXCLUSIVE)

Stallone starred in — and also directed — the action thriller “The Expendables” in 2010 alongside Jason Statham, Mickey Rourke and more. While filming a scene where Stallone got tackled by WWE legend Steve Austin, the stunt went wrong and left Stallone with dislocated shoulders and a fractured neck that required more than seven back surgeries. The “Rambo” actor needed a metal plate inserted into his neck and spinal fusions.

Popular on Variety

Stallone’s moral of the story is to “let other people do their job.” “Don’t be a stage hawk, or whatever you call it, a showboat. I know a lot of people are thinking about doing stunts … don’t. Don’t. Let the pro do it,” Stallone said. “You cannot beat gravity; when you hit the ground, you lose, and it’s going to come back.”

He continued, “I mean, just ask every football player in the world. So yeah, and people go, ‘Aren’t you proud of them?’ No. I think I’m an idiot for doing that. I’m proud that I broke myself in pieces. Like, duh, no.”

The actor shared a similar piece of advice ahead of the release of his memoir, “The Steps,” last month; Stallone told The New York Times that treating his body in the “masochistic” ways he did came “at a terrible price.” “If I could do it over again, I would say, ‘Let someone else carry the banner and don’t do your own stunts.”

Architectonic）以764万英镑（1010万美元）的价格成交，超过其250万英镑（330万美元）最高估值的三倍。该作品刷新了该艺术家的拍卖纪录，并在现场和电话竞标中经历了近八分钟的竞价。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "周三创下的其他纪录包括布里奇特·莱利（Bridget Riley）的《条纹2》（Streak Hepworth）的作品也刷新了纪录。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "西蒙收藏中最昂贵的作品——弗朗西斯·培根（Francis Bacon）的《运动中的人物》（Figure in Movement）——拍得1719万英镑（2280万美元），由现场的一位竞标者买下；而彼埃·蒙德里安（Piet Mondrian）的《双线与黄色的构成A》（Composition A, with Double Line and Yellow）则带来971万英镑（1286万美元）。胡安·米罗（Joan Miró）的《绘画（恋人——亚当与夏娃）》（Peinture (Les amants – Adam et Eve)）以856万英镑（1133万美元）售出，赫尔文·安德森（Hurvin Anderson）的《最后的房子》（Last House）在200万至300万英镑（260万至390万美元）的估价范围内拍得570万英镑（750万美元）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Fine Art Group主席兼创始人菲利普·霍夫曼（Philip Hoffman）在拍卖前对《ARTnews》表示，西蒙收藏中的少数几件作品将大幅领先，而其余大部分作品将在相对较少竞争的情况下售出。他说，弗里兹大师展的买家一直在保留资金，以期待这场拍卖。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "事后，霍夫曼称这两场拍卖清楚地表明市场稳健，不过他提醒不宜对总额作过分解读，特别是考虑到西蒙晚拍的41件拍品中有29件带有第三方担保，这意味着在竞标开始前，大部分财务风险就已经得到了消化。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他向《ARTnews》表示：“这些拍卖都是经过策划、管理，并且为了争取到最好的担保而被推到了极致。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当拍卖的最后两幅画作——格伦·利贡（Glenn Ligon）的《大银色在演艺界》（Large Silver In Show Business）和比阿特丽斯·米哈兹（Beatriz Milhazes）的《男孩》（O Rapaz (The Boy)）——分别以19.2万英镑（25万美元）的价格售出，而其最低估值分别为40万英镑（52.9万美元）和30万英镑（39.7万美元）时，全场一片寂静。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在20世纪/21世纪艺术晚拍开始前的短暂休息中，活力重现，两件约瑟夫·亚伯斯（Josef Albers）的作品超越了估价，紧接着勒内·马格里特（René Magritte）的《十六日》（Le seize septembre）拍得326万英镑（430万美元），远高于其180万英镑（240万美元）的最高估值。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Francis-Bacons-Figure-in-Movement-fetched-17.19-million-22.75-million-selling-to-a-bidder-in-the-room.png?w=400", "alt": "", "caption": "弗朗西斯·培根（Francis Bacon）的《运动中的人物》（Figure in Movement）拍得1719万英镑（2275万美元），由现场的一位竞标者买下。图片由佳士得图片有限公司提供。", "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当大卫·霍克尼（David Hockney）的《狗画17》（Dog Painting 17）登台时，英国人的活力显露无遗。这幅画作首次亮相拍场，引发了掌声以及一场激烈的角逐，佳士得伦敦专家埃德蒙·弗兰西（Edmond Francey）与至少三位通过电话竞标的其他专家参与其中。它最终拍得351万英镑（464万美元）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种爱国主义精神在英国画家弗洛拉·尤赫诺维奇（Flora Yukhnovich）的《随想曲》（Capriccio）中得以延续，该作品拍得220万英镑（290万美元），高于150万英镑（198万美元）的最高估值。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但当蒙德里安的《构成III》（Composition III (1920)）售出时，全场陷入寂静，观众和竞标者纷纷拿出相机记录下该画作以2520万英镑（3340万美元）成交的时刻，这一价格恰好落在他2000万至3000万英镑（2650万至3970万美元）估价的中间位置。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管这幅蒙德里安作品在拍卖前被预期会拍出最高价，但康定斯基的《多彩的生活》却证明了它才是更大的吸睛点。拍卖师阿德里安·迈耶（Adrien Meyer）将其描述为“该艺术家有史以来现身拍场的最重要的早期作品”。近20轮竞价在全场此起彼伏，佳士得专家阿梅利亚·沃克（Amelia Walker）、凯瑟琳·阿诺德（Katharine Arnold）和玛丽亚·洛斯（Maria Los）纷纷为这件作品展开争夺。最终，洛斯以2700万英镑（3570万美元）的落槌价拿下这幅画，在2500万英镑的最高估价之上，将最终成交价推至3156万英镑（4179万美元）。这幅画已于2023年返还给海德薇格·莱文斯坦-韦耶曼（Hedwig Lewenstein-Weyermann）的继承人。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正如第一场拍卖一样，气氛在临近尾声时再度发生了变化。在拍到第27件拍品——最终以150万英镑（198万美元）成交的安迪·沃霍尔的《蒙娜丽莎（反转系列）》（Mona Lisa (Reversal Series)）时，迈耶走下了拍卖台，由王郁歌（Yu Ge Wang）接替主持。随之而来的是一段艰难的胶着期，赛·托姆布莱（Cy Twombly）、乔治·康多（George Condo）、阿尔贝托·贾科梅蒂（Alberto Giacometti）和卢西安·弗洛伊德（Lucian Freud）等人的作品均遭遇流拍。到了晚上8点52分，由擦得发亮的男士乐福鞋和设计师手袋构成的海洋开始逐渐散去。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "就连慈善事业也未能完全盘活全场。伊格沙安·亚当斯（Igshaan Adams）由珠子、线和纺织品制成的雕塑作品《成为一朵玫瑰的笃定（二）》（The certainty of being a rose (ii)）拍得9.6万英镑（12.7万美元），尽管拍卖师提醒竞买人所得收益将捐赠给环保慈善机构。不过，这一结果依然创下了该艺术家的拍卖纪录。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "第二场拍卖按件数计算的成交率为85%，远低于西蒙收藏专场的98%。然而，凭借两件成交价超过2500万英镑的作品，两场合并的业绩让佳士得在11月17日开幕的纽约拍卖之前有充足的理由进行庆祝。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对霍夫曼而言，当晚的结果令人鼓舞但未必具有决定性，且大量使用第三方担保的情况也应持保留态度。他补充说，自己正在等待安东尼奥·霍姆·桑纳abend（Antonio Homem Sonnabend）收藏专场的拍卖——该专场估价超过5000万美元且不提供担保——以便对市场做出更清晰的判断。", "translated": true}]

content.article_text:
Christie’s London brought in £218.6 million ($289.4 million) across two evening sales Wednesday, more than doubling last year’s total and offering an encouraging sign for the art market ahead of the New York auctions next month.

Seven auction records were set, including five during the sale of British businessman Peter Simon’s collection, while a Wassily Kandinsky painting fetched £31.6 million ($41.8 million) in the evening’s second auction. (All prices reported include buyer’s premium.) Related Articles At Frieze, an Artist Project in the Fair's Public Toilets Confronts the UK's Ongoing Bathroom Wars Christie's to Sell Barbara Hepworth Sculpture Featured in Vogue Portrait by Lee Miller

The two sales, which coincide with Frieze London and Frieze Masters, achieved a combined sell-through rate of 91 percent by lot and 96 percent by value. The Simon collection, which several market insiders described to ARTnews as the real attraction in London this week, accounted for £107.5 million ($142.3 million) of the total, making it the highest-value single-owner collection ever sold at Christie’s London. The subsequent 20th- and 21st-century sale brought in £111.1 million ($147 million).

There was, however, some confusion about when the festivities were supposed to begin. Although the Simon sale started at 6 p.m., in some places Christie’s live-auction website advertised a 7 p.m. start time. At least three market professionals, including an adviser with a global clientele, had understood that the sale would begin at the later hour. Whether the hiccup caused anyone to miss bidding remains unclear.

Even still, Christie’s was packed when the “Monsoon: The Peter Simon Collection” sale began. Assembled by the founder British retailer Monsoon who has appeared on each edition of ARTnews ’s Top 200 Collectors list since 2005, the collection sold 98 percent by lot and 99 percent by value, with only one of the 41 works failing to find a buyer.

One of the evening’s biggest surprises came from Russian avant-garde painter Liubov Popova, whose Painterly Architectonic sold for £7.64 million ($10.1 million), more than three times its £2.5 million ($3.3 million) high estimate. Setting a new auction record for the artist, the work saw nearly eight minutes of bidding both in the room and on the phones.

Other records set Wednesday came for Bridget Riley’s Streak 2 , which £5.21 million ($6.9 million), and David Bomberg’s San Miguel, Toledo, Afternoon , which brought £3.26 million ($4.32 million). The bidding for the Bomberg work had the room cheering, and the auctioneer even asked for a closer inspection of the painting. Further records were achieved for Portia Zvavahera and Barbara Hepworth.

The Simon collection’s most expensive work, Francis Bacon’s Figure in Movement , fetched £17.19 million ($22.8 million), selling to a bidder in the room, while Piet Mondrian’s Composition A, with Double Line and Yellow brought £9.71 million ($12.86 million). Joan Miró’s Peinture (Les amants – Adam et Eve) sold for £8.56 million ($11.33 million), and Hurvin Anderson’s Last House brought £5.7 million ($7.5 million) against an estimate of £2 million–£3 million ($2.6 million–$3.9 million).

Philip Hoffman, chairman and founder of the Fine Art Group, told ARTnews before the sale that a handful of works in Simon’s collection would race ahead while much of the rest would sell with relatively little competition. Buyers at Frieze Masters, he said, had been holding back money in anticipation of the auction.

Afterward, Hoffman called the two sales a clear indication of a solid market, though he cautioned against reading too much into the totals, especially since 29 of the 41 lots in the Simon evening sale carried third-party guarantees, meaning much of the financial risk had already been accounted for before bidding began.

“These auctions are staged, managed, and already pumped up to the max for the best guarantees they can get,” he told ARTnews .

By the time the auction’s final two paintings, Glenn Ligon’s Large Silver In Show Business and Beatriz Milhazes’s O Rapaz (The Boy) , each sold for £192,000 ($250,000) against low estimates of £400,000 ($529,000) and £300,000 ($397,000), respectively, the room was mute.

In the short break before the 20th/21st Century evening sale, the energy returned, with two Josef Albers works exceeding their estimates, followed by René Magritte’s Le seize septembre , fetching £3.26 million ($4.3 million), well above its £1.8 million ($2.4 million) high estimate.

The zing of the Brits could be felt when David Hockney’s Dog Painting 17 came under the hammer. The painting, appearing at auction for the first time, prompted applause and a spirited contest involving Christie’s London specialist Edmond Francey and at least three other specialists bidding by telephone. It eventually fetched £3.51 million ($4.64 million).

The patriotic spirit continued with British painter Flora Yukhnovich’s Capriccio , which fetched £2.2 million ($2.9 million), against a high estimate of £1.5 million ($1.98 million).

But silence fell over the room for Mondrian’s Composition III (1920), as spectators and bidders alike took out their cameras to record the moment the painting sold for £25.2 million ($33.4 million), squarely in the middle of its £20 million–£30 million ($26.5 million–$39.7 million) estimate.

Though the Mondrian was expected to achieve the highest price going into the auction, Kandinsky’s Das bunte Leben proved to be the bigger attraction. Auctioneer Adrien Meyer described it as “the most important early work by the artist to ever come to auction.” Nearly 20 bids ricocheted across the room, with Christie’s specialists Amelia Walker, Katharine Arnold, and Maria Los competing for the work. Los ultimately secured the painting on a £27 million ($35.7 million) hammer bid, bringing the final price to £31.56 million ($41.79 million), against a £25 million high estimate. The painting had been restituted to the heirs of Hedwig Lewenstein-Weyermann in 2023.

As with the first sale, the mood changed again toward the end of the auction. At the 27th lot, Warhol’s Mona Lisa (Reversal Series) , which ultimately sold for £1.5 million ($1.98 million), Meyer stepped away from the rostrum and Yu Ge Wang took over. What followed was a difficult stretch, with works by Cy Twombly, George Condo, Alberto Giacometti, and Lucian Freud among those failing to find buyers. By 8:52 p.m., the sea of polished loafers and designer handbags had started to disappear.

Even a charitable cause could not entirely revive the room. Igshaan Adams’s The certainty of being a rose (ii) , a sculpture made of beads, thread and textile, fetched £96,000 ($127,000) despite the auctioneer reminding bidders that proceeds would benefit environmental charities. The result nevertheless established an auction record for the artist.

The second sale finished with an 85 percent sell-through rate by lot, well below the Simon collection’s 98 percent. Yet with two works selling for more than £25 million, the combined results gave Christie’s plenty to celebrate ahead of its New York sales, which begin November 17.

For Hoffman, the evening’s results were encouraging but not necessarily conclusive, and the extensive use of guarantees should be taken with a grain of salt. He added that he waiting for the sale of the Antonio Homem Sonnabend collection, estimated to bring more than $50 million and offered without guarantees, for a clearer reading of the market.

content.article_text:
Academy CEO Bill Kramer is set to make his first trip to Asia later this month. He will collect a leadership award at the Tokyo International Film Festival and also sit down with Toho president and CEO Matsuoka Hiro for a public conversation.

The festival’s 39th edition runs Oct. 26–Nov. 4 and has built a program titled Academy in Tokyo around the visit. Two colleagues will join Kramer in the Japanese capital: Academy president Lynette Howell Taylor and Meredith Shea, the organization’s chief membership, impact and industry officer.

Related Stories

ABC Orders Drama Pilot 'Rabbit' Based on U.K. Series 'Ludwig' From Megan Ganz & Humphrey Ker

ABC Alleges FCC's Attempts to Curb Its Free Speech Were Designed to Evade Judicial Review

The three executives will share a stage on Oct. 28 at Tokyo Midtown Hibiya Hall for a 90-minute panel moderated by TIFF festival director Hisamatsu Takeo. They will take the audience behind the curtain of the Oscars and outline the Academy’s international initiatives and membership programs. The conversation will also turn to how the organization views international cinema today and where it is heading.

Popular on Variety

Once the panel wraps, Kramer will receive TIFF’s Global Cinema Leadership Special Award. The festival said the honor recognizes his contribution to the growth of the worldwide film business and to film culture. Later that day, the Academy will hold a private reception for its members from across the globe.

Kramer returns to the same venue on Oct. 29 to sit down with Matsuoka. Their session will look at the state of the global film landscape and the outlook for theatrical and streaming distribution, along with ways to deepen cross-border partnerships. Both public events are free, though advance reservations are required. Booking details have yet to be released.

Kramer took the Academy’s top job in 2022. Before that, he ran the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures as its director and president. The museum opened its doors in September 2021. As CEO, Kramer has pushed to broaden the Academy’s 11,000-strong membership and give it a more international makeup. He runs the organization’s global operations, from the Oscars and the Academy Foundation to the $500 million Academy100 campaign.

Howell Taylor is in her second term as president. She is an Oscar-nominated producer whose credits include “A Star Is Born,” “The Accountant,” “Captain Fantastic” and “Blue Valentine.” She joined the Academy’s Producers Branch in 2014. She also co-produced the 92nd Oscars telecast in 2020, which earned her an Emmy nomination.

Shea is the first person to hold her post. Her remit covers membership, awards administration and talent development. It also includes the Academy’s outreach to film festivals and international territories.

Matsuoka has steered Toho’s expansion overseas, including its acquisitions of Gkids and Anime Limited. He also oversaw the production of Oscar winner “Godzilla Minus One.” In 2025, Toho posted its best-ever results at the Japanese box office. Matsuoka also sits on the board of trustees of the Academy Museum.

TIFFCOM, the content market that runs alongside the festival, takes place Oct. 28–30.

content.article_text:
Everybody to Kenmure Street ’s bid for Oscar recognition is gaining traction. The film directed by Felipe Bustos Sierra earned a spot on the influential DOC NYC short list of the year’s best documentaries announced on Wednesday. And on Tuesday, the film from executive producer Emma Thompson earned four nominations for the Critics Choice Documentary Awards , including Best Documentary Feature and Best Director.

Bustos Sierra’s film captures a remarkable event that took place in Glasgow, Scotland on May 13, 2021. Early that morning, immigration enforcement agents from the Home Office attempted to grab two Sikh men in a dawn raid but when locals became aware of what was going on they intervened, leading to an extraordinary standoff between law enforcement and members of the community in and around Kenmure Street.

Related Stories

‘Ghost In The Machine’ Rings Alarm Bell About AI, Explores How Tech Is Fundamentally Biased – For The Love Of Docs

Doc Talk Podcast: Producer James Costa On Deadline’s For The Love Of Docs Series, Oscar Season And ‘NAZA’ Controversy

Uniformed officers probably were unaware of the history of that neighborhood and of Glasgow as a whole and how residents there view immigrants.

Watch on Deadline

“This is a welcoming place… The south side of Glasgow has been a landing space for immigrants for centuries, since it was created really, [with] working class and immigrants living together,” the filmmaker said after a screening of the film as part of Deadline’s For the Love of Docs event series. “Glasgow has always been seen as a bit of a rebel city… And that history obviously permeates that neighborhood.”

The first person to try to disrupt the attempted immigration raid came to be known as “Van Man.” That individual climbed under the immigration vehicle in which the detainees were being held and latched onto the rear axle. Eventually, as word spread, hundreds of people poured into the street, many recording the events with their cell phone cameras. It became an enormous undertaking for Bustos Sierra and his editor Colin Monie to synchronize all that footage.

“It was the hardest part of making this film,” Bustos Sierra conceded. “The entire protest is shown… through what people had at hand on the day. We were lucky that two people who lived on the street were professional cameramen and they started filming on the smartphones, but… they went back, got their 4K cameras and managed to capture the second half of the day. But most of it is smartphone cameras and some really bad, some really old ones too.”

He added that some of the video came from activists who had scrubbed the metadata, “which made it really difficult to create an accurate timeline, which we eventually got to, but that was months of work.”

Emma Thompson not only executive produced the film, but she stars in it, in a manner of speaking — playing Van Man. That inventive choice came about after the real van man (who preferred to remain anonymous) said his words from interviews with the director could be used in the film, but he didn’t want to appear in it himself.

“Luckily, I had kept a light correspondence with Emma Thompson after my first film came out about Chile, a country that she has also a strong connection with,” Bustos Sierra explained. “And so, when Van Man told me didn’t want to be in it… you think, ‘What do I have?’ …And I just pictured Emma Thompson going out there and saying, ‘Hey, I’m Van Man.’ It made me laugh like maybe what Van Man did [for] the protest, Emma will do for our film.”

The dramatized sequence, shot in London, involved Thompson climbing onto a rig beneath a van. She was wedged in there like the real guy in Glasgow.

“We did build the rig. We did put her under underneath the van. When she did arrive, she looked at the rig, looked at me and [cinematographer] Kirsten [McMahon] and say, ‘This is the strangest thing anyone’s ever asked me to do.’ …I think she made the discomfort part of her performance. And so, it worked really well.”

Bustos Sierra sees what the people around Kenmure Street did that day as “small revolutionary acts.” He describes their attitude as, “You don’t remove [these men] without valid cause as this was happening. There’s absolutely nothing illegal [done] by these two guys. These are our neighbors and we’re just going to stand for our community.”

Watch the full conversation in the video above.

For The Love of Docs is produced with the long-time support of National Geographic Documentary Films. Films are presented free of charge to the audience and to the filmmakers. The series continues with weekly screenings, followed by conversations with filmmakers through December 1. Join us next week for Seized , directed by Sharon Liese, the story of a police raid on a small-town newspaper in Kansas that triggered a national uproar. To RSVP for the screening, click here .

The 5th Floorでは、韓国の 東豆川 を拠点に活動するアーティスト・コレクティブ、 AfroAsia Collective （アフロアジア・コレクティヴ）の展覧会「ポータル：アフロアジア」を開催する。 AfroAsia Collective は、キュレーターの サン・ア・ムーン （1985年韓国・ソウル生まれ）とアーティスト・映画作家の チェ・ウォンジュン （1979年韓国・ソウル生まれ）によって2021年に設立された、アフリカおよびアジアの移民コミュニティと関わりながら活動するアーティスト・コレクティブ。1955年にインドネシアのバンドンでアジア・アフリカの29カ国が集まり、植民地主義に反対し連帯を掲げたアジア・アフリカ会議（バンドン会議）の精神を受け継ぎ、東豆川の「Space AfroAsia」を拠点に、現代美術をとおしてアフリカとアジアのあいだの新たな文化的連帯の形成を目指している。これまでのプロジェクトに、ナイジェリアのミュージシャンOsinachiとの音楽コラボレーション（2021–2023）、韓国におけるアフリカ出身者のコミュニティを探るドキュメンタリー《Dongducheon New Town》（2023）、韓国の若者とアフリカ出身の移民の若者がともに取り組むK-popプロジェクト《AfroZia》（2024）などがある。また、グループ展「 PANORAMA 」（ソンウン・アートスペース、ソウル、2025）に参加し、リウム美術館の連続プログラム「 Prime Meridian Unconference 」（ソウル、2025）でトークを行なったほか、カリフォルニア大学デービス校マネッティ・シュレム美術館（2024）、ニューヨーク大学アフリカ・アフリカン・ディアスポラ研究センター（CSAAD、2025）、ハーバード大学（2025）のパブリック・プログラムで作品が上映・紹介されている。

韓国における米軍基地村は、長年にわたり冷戦をめぐる地政学とその軍事秩序によって形づくられてきた。しかし今日、これらの場所は、アフリカ出身の移民コミュニティにとって、新たな移住、定住、文化交流の空間へと変容しつつある。本展は、米軍基地村として知られる東豆川の 保山洞 と 坡州 に焦点を当て、歴史記録やアーカイブ資料、地域のコミュニティの人々のポートレート、ストリートや日常の風景を捉えた写真をとおして、軍事的な必要性から形成された空間が、新たな社会関係やコミュニティの生まれる場へと変化していく過程をたどる。 タイトルにある「ポータル」とは、異なる場所と時間、歴史と経験が交差し、新たな関係が生まれる通路を指す。本展は「アフロアジア・フューチャリズム」を、アフリカとアジアの美学の単純な融合ではなく、植民地主義、軍事化、排除という歴史の交差をもつアフリカとアジアのあいだの連帯から、新たな共同性と未来を生み出すための方法論および実践として提示しようとする。

content.article_text:
More than 45 years after the first Friday the 13th , Brad Caleb Kane is righting a wrong from the set of the 1980 slasher.

Ahead of Friday’s Crystal Lake premiere on Peacock , the series creator noted that a snake Pamela Voorhees (Linda Cardellini) sets free after finding it in the camp pantry in the first episode is “a direct nod” to a trained serpent that was actually killed while filming the original movie.

“But [Pam’s] a different person in the first episode than the kids are [in the movie],” he explained. “Yes, it’s a direct nod, but then it goes to the place of the first movie.”

Related Stories

Brad Caleb Kane Found It “Hard” Ignoring ‘Crystal Lake’ Fan Theories, Teases “Certain Explanations” Given In Prequel: “It’s Grounded In Reality”

Linda Cardellini Admits She “Wanted” To Recreate Pamela Voorhees’ Haircut For ‘Crystal Lake’: “We Tried It For A Second”

Kane clarified: “But we don’t actually kill a snake in ours. No, no animals were harmed in the making of Crystal Lake . Some hippies might have been harmed in the making of Crystal Lake , but no animals.”

Watch on Deadline

During the filming of the original 1980 slasher Friday the 13th , a domesticated bull snake was infamously killed in real life while shooting the scene in which “final girl” Alice (Adrienne King) finds the reptile slithering around her cabin and calls for her fellow counselors to come help.

RELATED: 2026-27 Premiere Dates For New & Returning Series On Broadcast, Streaming & Cable

In the scene, Bill (Harry Crosby) runs in with a machete and kills the snake, before it’s shown writhing and dying on the floor. Cast and crew have since revealed that the sequence was real , noting that the snake’s handler was unaware of the film’s intentions and was “inconsolable” afterward.

With PETA launching two months before Friday the 13th ‘s premiere in 1980, there were no animal protection laws in place yet during the filming of the Sean S. Cunningham-helmed movie.

Streaming Friday on Peacock, Crystal Lake stars Linda Cardellini as Pam Voorhees, who struggles to grieve after her son Jason drowned the summer before. As two strangers begin digging into her mysterious past, Pam goes to murderous lengths to keep her secrets buried.

content.article_text:
Joseph Zada and Mckenna Grace have begun their international press tour to promote their movie, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping .

The duo kicked things off in Sydney, the home country of Zada, who plays young Haymitch Abernathy.

Grace will play tribute Maysilee Donner in the film, set for U.S. release on November 20, 2026.

RELATED: Everything We Know About The ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Movie So Far

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is directed by Francis Lawrence from a screenplay by Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie, based on the adaptation and novel by Suzanne Collins.

The film follows sixteen-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Zada) from District 12, beginning on the morning of the reaping for the 50th Annual Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell, the biggest Games yet with twice as many tributes.

Set in the world of Panem 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games , the story follows Haymitch into the arena, where he forms an unlikely alliance with fellow tribute Maysilee Donner (Grace) and joins a coalition determined to challenge the Capitol’s control under President Snow (Ralph Fiennes).

As the competition unfolds, Haymitch risks everything to take down the Games from within the arena — setting in motion the rebellion that will change Panem forever.

RELATED: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Trailer: Joseph Zada Stores Up Fury For The Revolution As Colorful Creatures Attack In The Arena

The cast includes Joseph Zada, Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Mckenna Grace, Maya Hawke, Whitney Peak, Kelvin Harrison Jr., Ben Wang. Other actors featured include Jesse Plemons, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Maya Hawke, Whitney Peak, and Kelvin Harrison Jr.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Nina Jacobson, Brad Simpson and Francis Lawrence.

RELATED: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Red Carpet Photos: All Of Zendaya & Tom Holland’s Looks From Press Tour

content.article_text:
Fatalism, self-determination and imagination all gently wrestle for control of the narrative(s) in “ Beach Fictions ,” an enchanting and subtly profound diptych that follows one young woman through two diverging versions of the same day — saying much in the process about the voices, inner and otherwise, that we grant most control in our lives, for better or worse. Though its structuring principle of a single day playing out twice consecutively to differing effect (as opposed to braiding its alternate timelines like “Sliding Doors” or “Blind Chance”) explicitly recalls Hong Sangsoo’s “Right Now, Wrong Then,” this chicly poised debut feature by fellow South Korean Lim Hayeon has a style, tone and outlook of its own, maintained with impressive control over a surprisingly breezy-feeling 145 minutes.

Related Stories

Peacock App Launches 'Your Bravoverse,' Featuring a Personalized TikTok-Style Video Feed Hosted by AI-Generated Andy Cohen

One of the real discoveries in this year’s main competition at the Busan Film Festival , “Beach Fictions” should have little difficulty charming other programmers on the international fest circuit following its world premiere — while only its running time, manageable but unexpectedly robust for a film this light on its feet, presents an obstacle to global arthouse distribution, or at least specialist streaming exposure. Either way, this graduation project (produced by the Korean Academy of Film Arts) announces its writer-director-editor as one to watch, should her future films match this one’s warmth and formal elegance; in only her second big-screen outing after years of TV work, winsome lead Hansol Park also feels like a breakout talent.

Popular on Variety

“Beach Fictions” pulls you in from its first iridescent frame, as Sinuk Park’s camera glides serenely from a bejeweled nighttime view of Incheon through the chattery hubbub of a mood-lit restaurant where Tae-ju (Park), seen only from behind, is dining with friends, their conversation seemingly more animated than hers. Even without the detached voiceover — which turns out to belong to perceptive novelist Ewha (Sujeong Ye), describing the superficial response of Tae-ju’s friends to an anecdote she shares — we’d sense her loneliness amid company. Later, when her friends abandon her at the table to smoke outside, she’s crushed to find them gossiping about her; shortly afterwards, in a never-rains-but-pours development, she breaks up with her casual boyfriend Hyun-jin after he expresses scant interest in taking the relationship further.

With her social life in tatters and a world of her anxieties realized, Tae-ju rashly skips town, heading for the tranquil coastal guesthouse of another friend. On the train there, she encounters Ewha, whom we’ve already seen observing her from afar at the restaurant, and confides in the kindly, silver-haired older woman — who says Tae-ju resembles the protagonist of the novel she’s currently writing. But is she the writer’s inspiration or her creation, an incomplete fiction who has somehow taken on an agency of her own? From here on out, the authorship of Tae-ju’s life is ambiguous, as well as constantly in flux, buffeted by the whims and suggestions of others, as well as by her own impulses.

In the sleepy beach town, she meets and is immediately entranced by charismatic street magician Manhyuk (Kim Wookyum, delightful), only to later be warned off him by her hostess, who claims he’s a local lothario and sometime sex worker. A day in his company turns sour but when, in the film’s deftly shuffled second half, she meets him in slightly different circumstances, and the day’s events take on a different chain of connections, the potential romantic outcome differs too.

Her nascent relationship with Manhyuk is the chief variable of Tae-ju’s two stories, but other, slighter factors push it this way and that: a water-damaged phone in need of repair; a hangout with fellow guesthouse patrons that echoes or corrects her earlier social fallout; and a consultation with a psychic, recommended by Ehwa, whose counsel also shifts her fate. The contrasts between the two tales are never drastic; the gradations are sometimes as fine as those between warm and cool melancholy. The camerawork is consistently, richly sun-flooded, but some compositions isolate Tae-ju more than others; Wonhong Lee’s delicate jazz piano score can similarly tilt a situation from cozy to nervy.

But both gently lolloping narratives hold the attention, in large part thanks to Park’s deeply sympathetic performance as Hae-ju, simultaneously played as a fragile, will-o’-the-wisp go-alonger — or perhaps just an author’s as-yet-unformed blank canvas — and a wounded flesh-and-blood human now guarding her emotions more carefully. It’s a canny turn completely in synch with Lim’s complex, metatextual script, which brims with ideas about the fictional construction process, as well the real-life bind felt by vulnerable young women expected to bend to others’ desires and expectations. Is life itself not just a series of drafts and redrafts, with notes we either learn from or don’t, our characters never not in progress? Wry and wise and happy-sad, “Beach Fictions” crosses nothing out, alive to all possibilities.

content.article_text:
Looks like “ Artificial ” is the real thing.

Luca Guadagnino’s genre-blending movie about the evils of artificial intelligence (and one of its fathers, Sam Altman) had a triumphant U.K. premiere at the London Film Festival on Sunday. The director, standing beside key cast members Andrew Garfield and Yura Borisov, received thunderous applause at Royal Festival Hall.

The British event followed the world premiere of “Artificial” a week earlier at the New York Film Festival. It was a make-or-break moment for a project plagued by scandal after Amazon MGM punted the film off its summer slate. Worse was what came after: an odious whisper campaign saying the film stank (anonymous sources dismissed it as only worthy of a streaming release, according to a July report). But the Big Apple swallowed the film with rapture.

Related Stories

‘Always Lalisa’ Director Sue Kim Reveals Secrets Behind Lisa Doc, From YG Blocking Blackpink Music to Lots of Tequila Shots

Dawn Porter to Direct Documentary on Pioneering TV News Anchor Max Robinson

“So this is a dawn-of-a-new-world story, as well as a backstabbing corporate business story, and also a horror movie, in which AI emerges from the lab as a sinister serpent,” wrote Variety chief critic Owen Gleiberman in his review, calling the movie a “brilliant but playful docudrama, meticulously true to history.”

Popular on Variety

Others agree. The title has a 96% Fresh rating on review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes, representing the highest score of Guadagnino’s career across 11 feature film releases. Garfield has been catapulted to the front of the best supporting actor race, thanks to a performance that delivers “a masterclass in diabolical villainy,” according to another review.

The notices, the standing ovations, the awards buzz — all of it represents a stunning reversal of fortune for Guadagnino after the Amazon debacle in June. It was highly uncommon, in Hollywood terms, for even a tech-owned content studio to kill a project it had cradled since infancy. Neon rescued the movie with a global rights deal shortly after the Amazon rift.

“We believe that ‘Artificial’ will be better served if it were released by a different studio,” the e-commerce giant said at the time. Global press almost unanimously noted that the decision to jettison the movie came only three months after Amazon signed a significant partnership with Altman’s OpenAI (including a $50 billion investment in the company).

But, per Variety’ s sources, the writing is on the wall. Nothing was wrong with “Artificial,” and the response underlines the dubiousness of Amazon’s decision to drop it.

“Wasn’t this supposed to be god-awful?” wondered one film executive at a rival studio. The exec didn’t just raise an eyebrow at Amazon MGM, but at other legacy distributors who were in the mix to take the project before Neon won out. “A reaction this strong just shows you, every studio pretending the film wasn’t releasable is just conflicted out by their own investments in AI.”

In July, New York magazine published a piece citing individuals close to the project as saying it “lacked theater-worthy criteria.” That doesn’t quite track with early audience response. In fact, the critical consensus is that “Artificial” — not Aaron Sorkin’s “The Social Reckoning,” which debuted last weekend via Sony Pictures — is a worthy spiritual successor to David Fincher’s “The Social Network.” It’s hard to imagine Amazon not being pleased with this response had it kept “Artificial.”

Interestingly, Amazon’s headaches at the intersection of talent and AI are not exclusive to the Guadagnino movie. At New York Comic Con last weekend, actor Nicolas Cage made waves when he disclosed that he refused to sign a document permitting the studio to use AI in and around his likeness on its now-canceled original series “Spider-Noir.”

“I am not an AI-friendly actor. I’m not a member of their club. I didn’t sign the waiver,” Cage said. “I’m probably not going to be working with that studio again.” There’s a bit more to this story, insiders close to “Spider-Noir” said. Cage was referring to a form from the show’s producer, Sony Pictures Television, considered “industry standard” on content shoots. The waiver gives the studio permission to create a duplicate of an actor in costume, which aids in VFX work during postproduction. Actors are free to opt out, and the form is said to be in line with SAG-AFTRA guidelines.

But it won’t be the end of talent bristling over the coming AI revolution — at Amazon or elsewhere. One creative team member on an Amazon MGM series tells Variety that AI training is a requirement on the lot these days.

The source describes a “mandatory and perfunctory meeting” with the company’s AI team, billed as standard workplace education that corporations regularly hold around sexual harassment and fire safety. The AI group spent an hour pitching the creatives on a suite of products it referred to as “tools.” Our source says, however, it became clear that these tools could “eliminate entire jobs” on the production. Amazon MGM declined to comment on the matter.

More telling, per the source, is that the show’s corporate stewards from Amazon also sat through the training “stone-faced.” While the individual won’t name the execs in attendance, they found it “collectively embarrassing for everyone to be doing this, including on the Amazon side.” A source with direct knowledge of Amazon’s process said such meetings are not mandatory, and humans guide every part of the process related to the tools.

And so begins the great sacrifice the major studios are about to make in service of computer-based cost efficiencies and the “move fast and break things” bravado of Silicon Valley. Time will tell if a prompt can make content that’s as buzzy and well positioned as “Artificial.”

content.article_text:
George Osborne, chairman of the British Museum , has expressed hope that a deal can be struck to share the Parthenon Marbles between Athens and London, despite the two-centuries-long diplomatic feud.

“I’m still optimistic that we can reach an agreement,” Osborne told reporters in Athens on Tuesday. “If everyone enters into it with the spirit of we’re not going to get everything we want, as is always the case with a successful agreement, then there’s a deal to be done.” Related Articles Greek Prime Minister to "Ramp Up" Efforts Related to Parthenon Marbles Return The British Museum Will Extend Its Hours Amid 'Extraordinary' Demand for Bayeux Tapestry

The Parthenon Marbles , made between 447 and 432 BCE by the Greek sculptor Phidias, depict gods and processions in marble relief panels, sculptures, and friezes. They’re also known as the Elgin Marbles, after the Scottish nobleman Lord Elgin, who was the British ambassador to Constantinople. Elgin removed the sculptures from the Acropolis in Athens in 1801, while Greece was under Ottoman occupation. He later sold the sculptures to the British government, which has housed them in the British Museum ever since.

Greece has sought the marbles’ return since gaining independence from the Ottoman Empire in 1832, arguing that Elgin had no legal grounds to remove them. British officials, meanwhile, have cited the British Museum Act 1963, which prohibits the museum from deaccessioning objects in its collection, as justification for retaining the sculptures. Tensions between the two countries have escalated in recent years, fueled by the opening of a dedicated museum for the marbles in Athens and reports of leaks and other preservation concerns in the British Museum’s galleries.

“I very much hope we can come to some arrangement whereby the Parthenon sculptures that are in London can be seen in Athens but they have to be shared,” Osborne said Tuesday. “I know that’s not the position of everyone in Greece, and I understand that and respect that, but that is our position, and so if we want to make progress, it has to be in that spirit.”

Osborne’s comments follow a September op-ed by Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis published in the Guardian , in which he took issue with British Museum director Nicholas Cullinan’s characterization of France’s loan of the Bayeux Tapestry as “a very compelling example of international partnership.” Cullinan had suggested that a similar model of “reciprocal exchange” could be applied to the Parthenon Marbles.

“Nobody would seriously contemplate cutting what survives of the tapestry in two and displaying half in London and half in Bayeux, and claiming this was an adequate way to understand it,” he writes, “Yet that is exactly what happened to the Parthenon sculptures.”

Osborne, a former Chancellor of the Exchequer, has been at the forefront of negotiations between the British Museum and Greece. In 2023, the London institution confirmed that it had been in talks with the Acropolis Museum, saying it was close to finalizing a deal under which the sculptures would return to Greece over time as part of a cultural exchange. The agreement never materialized. Greek Culture Minister Lina Mendoni told reporters days later that Greece would not accept a deal affirming the United Kingdom’s ownership claim. Instead, she proposed an exchange that would ensure treasures from Greek antiquity, including objects of comparable prestige to the Parthenon Marbles, would remain on display in London.

World leaders are set to convene at the EU-UK summit in Brussels next month. Speaking at a conference at the University of Athens on October 6, Mitsotakis suggested that discussions on diplomatic ties between the European Union and the United Kingdom, which voted to leave the bloc in 2016, would involve the British Museum dispute.

“The Parthenon sculptures will be part of this debate. This is not just an issue for Greece, it’s an issue for Europe,” Mitsotakis said.

content.article_text:
It’s hard to imagine the American Film Institute ‘s board of directors without Bob Daly , but that will be the case as of next week. The former CBS and Warner Bros boss is stepping down after 17 years as its chairman — and 45 as a trustee.

Daly, who first joined the board in 1981, will exit the top post at the October 21 board meeting, where a successor will be discussed.

Related Stories

The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office

The 30 Highest-Grossing Animated Films Of All Time At The Global Box Office

“In a career that brought me from running CBS to Warner Bros to the Los Angeles Dodgers, I can honestly say that serving as Chairman of the AFI Board of Directors has been one of the greatest honors of my career,” Daly said in a statement. “This is a board that represents all aspects of the film and television communities, and to see they come together with a shared passion for the art form has been a wonder to behold. Long live the AFI.”

A rep for AFI said Daly, who joined the board in April 1981, is stepping down to pass the torch to the next generation.

Watch on Deadline

RELATED: ‘Blazing Saddles’ Named Funniest Film Of All Time By AFI In Honor Of Mel Brooks’ 100th Birthday

Daly began his career at CBS, where he spent 25 years. He joined Warner Bros in 1980 and served as chairman and co-CEO with Terry Semel for nearly two decades. The pair were credited with 16 consecutive years of record earnings. Daly then was chairman and CEO of the Dodgers, the MLB team then-owned by News Corp. He also was chairman of the Save the Children board for five years.

“Leadership is an art in itself – and in that regard, Mr. Daly is a master,” AFI President and CEO Bob Gazzale said. “Over the past 40 years, no single person has had a greater impact on AFI’s work in preservation, celebration and education than Bob Daly.”

content.article_text:
Editor’s Note: This story originally appeared in On Balance , the ARTnews newsletter about the art market and beyond. Sign up here to receive it every Wednesday.

Industry Moves

Bortolami Now Represents Emily Sundblad: The New York–based painter and cofounder of Reena Spaulings Fine Art will have a work in the gallery’s booth at Art Basel Miami Beach in December. She will debut a theatrical production, made with Ken Okiishi, at the New Theater Hollywood in February.

Shigeo Otake Joins White Cube : Born and based in Kobe, Japan, the artist is known for his surrealist-inflected paintings featuring an array of otherworldly figures. He will debut new paintings at the gallery’s booth at Art Basel Paris ahead of a solo show at the Mason’s Yard space in spring 2028.

Olney Gleason Takes on Kour Pour: The artist, who draws on a range of visual traditions and his British and Iranian heritage, will have a solo show at the gallery in early 2027. He currently has works on view in its booth at Frieze London.

Hanna Hur Joins Greene Naftali: The Toronto-born, New York–based artist is currently showing a series of new paintings at the gallery. She was featured in the 2025 edition of the Made in L.A. biennial.

Alexander Berggruen Now Represents Raul de Lara: The sculptor is known for making handcrafted pieces in wood depicting flora and household objects. He recently made work for Hermès.

Jan Kaps Adds Lukas Luzius Leichtle to Its Roster: The artist, who is known for his hyper-realistic paintings of the human body, had a solo show at the Cologne-based gallery in June. He will display new work at its booth at Art Basel Paris.

Tanja Grunert and Fierman to Share Space in Chinatown: The two New York galleries, which are not merging, will retain their individual programs and artists but will rotate use of a gallery at 19 Pike Street. The first show will be a solo for Odette Steinert, opening November 13.

IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts Names New Director: Mary Deleary (Chippewas of the Thames First Nation)will begin in her role at the Santa Fe, New Mexico, institution on October 19. She is currently director of the IAIA Research Center for Contemporary Native Arts, which is also under the umbrella of the Institute of American Indian Arts (IAIA).

Chicago-Based Gertie Promotes Chanelle Lacy to Managing Director: Lacy has been with the company behind Chicago Exhibition Week since 2023. “Chanelle is a force, and this appointment is about recognizing that and giving her an even bigger platform,” founder Abby Pucker said in a statement.

Rubin Museum Gives Nearly $195,000 for Research Grants for Himalayan Art: The 2026 grant cycle received 250 letters of inquiry; the 13 grantees will receive between $3,000 and $25,000 for their individual projects. Artists chosen for the grant include Peldon Tshering, Sonam Tshedzom Tingkhye, and Tenzing Rigdol. The full list of winners can be for here .

The Big Number: $35 M.

That’s the high estimate for Amedeo Modigliani’s limestone sculpture Tête (1911–12). Though better known for his paintings of nude women with elongated figures and almond-shaped eyes, the artist also made around 28 sculptures during his lifetime. This “ fresh to the market ” work, which has not changed hands since 1972, “embodies everything that makes Modigliani’s sculpture so revered, including its profound art historical importance,” according to Phillips deputy chairman of the Americas and senior international specialist Jeremiah Evarts. The $35 million estimate is just above the price for the second-most expensive sculpture by the artist ever sold, another Tête that sold in 2019 for $34.3 million. His record for three-dimensional work stands at $52.8 million, while for painting, it’s $170.4 million, a benchmark set more than a decade ago, when Nu couché (1918) sold in 2015.

Read This.

Ahead of Frieze’s VIP opening today, the New York Times published a dispatch from Hong Kong about what goes into putting on an international fair of Frieze’s scale. But instead of talking to the fair director, reporter Mercedes Hutton zeroed in on the work that happens in “the shadows,” as she puts it—that is to say, the labor of one company specializing in logistics that takes care of building the crates for transporting an artwork to its next destination, whether by land, sea, or air. The most fascinating part of the article comes when Franck Vidal, the head of fabrication for Eythos, describes how he builds a crate, even for a work that isn’t quite finished. “To me, the journey starts on the screen or as data,” he says, beginning his explanation. It’s a worth reading on to see what comes next.

content.article_text:
On Tuesday, the Israel Antiquities Authority (IAA) returned 22 antiquities to Greece . The cache includes decorated pottery from the 8th through the 4th centuries BCE that had been seized during an illegal antiquities trafficking investigation in and around Tel Aviv in 2020.

The ceremony took place at the National Archaeological Museum in Athens and was attended by Lina Mendoni, the Greek Minister of Culture; Pninat Yanai, the Israeli Ambassador to Greece; and Amir Ganor, director of the IAA’s Anti Theft Prevention Unit. This handover marks the first time Israel has returned contested items to Greece.

In a social media post , the IAA states that the 2020 seizure involved raids of an unnamed gallery, warehouses, and apartments which uncovered “thousands of archaeological items from Israel and around the world.” The investigation was prompted by suspicion of looting at ancient sites in the Mediterranean. The IAA does not clarify why it took Israel six years to return the items to Greece, or if objects belonging to other nations are also in the process of being repatriated. It is also not clear from where in Greece the items were looted.

Among the items back on Greek soil are black- and red-figure vessels, some with handles, decorated with scenes from Greek mythology, and would have been used in everyday life or as burial offerings. Among the vases of varying shapes and sizes (15 Attic vessels and six Corinthian, according to the Jerusalem Post ) was a bronze female figure.

Lina Mendoni, the Greek Minister of Culture, said that “this return lays the foundation for deepening cooperation between our countries in the field of protecting cultural heritage. Every return of antiquities to their country of origin also carries with it a broad moral and symbolic significance.”

She added that the return, “reminds us all that protecting cultural heritage is a shared responsibility, and that the effective fight against the illegal trade in antiquities requires cooperation between countries, mutual trust, and a commitment to upholding the law and strengthening heritage.”
