content.article_text:
Films and events

Galas

Elsinore

Opening Night Gala

Andrew Scott is a towering presence in this singular account of Ian Charleson’s life, capturing the moment when he faced his own mortality as he prepared to play Hamlet at the Royal National Theatre.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Screening at cinemas around the UK – find out more .

Credits

Director Simon Stone

Screenwriter Stephen Beresford

With Andrew Scott, Olivia Colman, Billie Piper, Johnny Flynn, Luke Thompson

UK 2026. 104min

Courtesy of STUDIOCANAL

Language English

Access information

Wednesday 7 October 19:15

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Thursday 8 October 15:15

Relaxed screening – buy tickets for this screening

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Friday 9 October 15:00

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Friday 16 October 12:30

Audio description

Introduction

Simon Stone’s film, written by Stephen Beresford (Pride), details Ian Charleson’s decision to step into the National Theatre’s production of Hamlet following Daniel Day-Lewis’ departure. Scott, who so movingly portrayed a man wracked by grief in All of Us Strangers (LFF 2023), here ascends new heights with his performance. He captures the tumult and humanity of Charleson, who is dying of AIDS (his scenes with Olivia Colman’s doctor are a veritable masterclass in screen performance) while revealing the joyful process of co-creation and the importance of fellowship in embodying a character as complex as Shakespeare’s haunted Danish prince. With a stellar cast that also includes Billie Piper, Johnny Flynn, Juliet Stevenson, Adeel Akhtar and Peter Mullan, Elsinore skilfully shifts gear between the ebullience of rehearsals and performance, and the profound reality of life on the precipice of the unknown. It’s a stunning achievement by Stone (The Daughter, LFF 2015; The Dig, LFF 2021) who has crafted a stirring ode to an extraordinary life, the strength of community and resistance, and the triumph of art.

Kristy Matheson

Content advice

Contains scenes of sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Screen Talk: Andrew Scott

We welcome the versatile star of our Opening Night Gala, Elsinore, to discuss his extraordinary body of work across stage and screen.

The Debut

For LFF 2026’s curtain call, writer-director Jesse Eisenberg delivers a rapturous and raucously funny love letter to community theatre, featuring a luminous lead performance by Julianne Moore.

A Long Winter

Andrew Haigh’s sensitive drama transforms a snowbound landscape into a space where beauty and longing exist in delicate equilibrium.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Family

Iron Boy

Le Corset

With its smooth, hand-painted style, Iron Boy is a warm, moving animation about an 11-year-old boy who is forced to rethink his outlook on the world when he receives a life-changing diagnosis.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Louis Clichy

Screenwriters Louis Clichy, Franck Salomé

With Gary Clichy, Rod Paradot, Aurélie Vassort

France-Belgium 2026. 90min

Courtesy of Playtime

Language French With English subtitles

Access information

Friday 16 October 13:35

Live reading of subtitles (Headphones are available on request)

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Louis Clichy’s precise, handsomely produced tales finds young Christophe the subject of ridicule at school due to his issues with posture that make him appear ‘wonky’. A solution is found in the form of an iron brace. At first, it makes him feel like a robot and places him at odds with his proud father who questions his future on the family farm. But then he discovers the possibility of a different life.

Justin Johnson

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

A Mighty Adventure

This lovingly crafted, dialogue-free animated tale follows a trio of insects who undertake an epic journey.

Wildwood

A forest inhabited by magical beings is the setting for this epic stop-motion saga from LAIKA Studios.

My Friend the Sun

In this engrossing and brightly coloured animated triumph, a young girl is transported to the home of the Mexican gods and has to fight to find her way back home.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Journey

In the Shadows

Jasmine Jobson leads a brilliant ensemble in bringing the inspirational story of champion East End boxer Ramla Ali to the screen.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Anthony Wonke

Screenwriter Ursula Rani Sarma

With Jasmine Jobson, Finn Cole, Gershwyn Eustache Jnr

UK 2025. 117min

Courtesy of True Brit Entertainment

Languages English, Somali With some English subtitles

Certificate BBFC15

Access information

Friday 9 October 18:15

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Saturday 10 October 17:30

Descriptive subtitles

Friday 16 October 14:45

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Finding an unlikely passion for boxing as a teen, Ali defied the odds to become an international sporting icon. Director Anthony Wonke’s talents as an award-winning documentarian shine through here. Naturalistic production design, scripting and exceptional performances all chime in this compelling drama about a young woman determined to carve her own path whilst never losing sight of her past and community.

Kristy Matheson

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury and harm towards children.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

ANIMOL

Ashley Walters’ directorial debut, set in a young offenders institute, is a strikingly shot and sensitively made depiction of survival, surprise connections and redemption.

Congo Boy

Set in the Central African Republic, Rafiki Fariala’s melodic autobiographical feature follows a young refugee who, against all odds, chases his musical dreams.

FLORID

In this striking British feature debut, a young man living in supported accommodation tries to juggle his musical aspirations and mental health issues.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Dare

Everytime

Sandra Wollner’s film, winner of Un Certain Regard at Cannes this year, is an enigmatic exploration of grief and the path to healing.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Sandra Wollner

With Birgit Minichmayr, Tristan López, Lotte Shirin Keiling

Austria-Germany 2026. 124min

Courtesy of BFI Distribution

Language German With English subtitles

Introduction

In Wollner’s lyrical and haunting third feature, a mother, a daughter and a teenage boy struggle with blame and forgiveness over a recent tragedy that saw their lives intersect. To escape their daily surroundings, they travel to Tenerife. As the long days go by under the sun and heat, reality and memories blend as each grapples with their feelings and a desire to move forward.

Isabel Moir

With thanks to the Austrian Cultural Forum London.

Content advice

Contains scenes of drug use.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra

Jacqueline Lentzou follows Moon 66 Questions with this evocative and playful look into the life of a teenager who is completely unaware of the forces at play in her fate.

Josephine

Winner of the Grand Jury Dramatic Prize at Sundance, this suspenseful and devastating film follows a child trying to navigate life after witnessing a sexual assault.

Mouse

Katherine Mallen Kupferer and Sophie Okonedo excel in this moving drama about facing up to life in the aftermath of a tragedy.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Galas

Minotaur

Andrey Zvyagintsev transposes Claude Chabrol’s La Femme infidèle to contemporary Russia, delivering a magnificent political allegory that dissects the mechanics of ego, violence and corruption.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Screening at cinemas around the UK – find out more .

Credits

Director Andrey Zvyagintsev

Screenwriters Simon Lyashenko, Andrey Zvyagintsev

With Dmitriy Mazurov, Iris Lebedeva, Boris Kudrin, Yuriy Zavalnyouk, Varvara Zmykova

France-Germany-Latvia 2026. 141min

Courtesy of MUBI

Language Russian With English subtitles

Certificate LFF18

Access information

Friday 16 October 17:45

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Saturday 17 October 20:00

Descriptive subtitles

Sunday 18 October 20:00

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

At the onset of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Gleb, a powerful CEO, is preoccupied with feeding the war machine with workers, when he learns of his wife’s infidelity. Faced with this discovery and a complex professional decision, his scruples quickly fade. Zvyagintsev’s masterful and darkly humorous tale of impunity will make your blood run cold.

Diana Cipriano

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, nudity, and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Mariinka

Shot over ten years, this unflinching portrait of youth in Eastern Ukraine is a rare and powerful account of the passing of time during conflict.

Imperium

Master of archival film reconstruction, Sergei Loznitsa, reframes Soviet history once again via the revealing gaze of Italian cameramen who captured life there in the early 1970s.

Fjord

This searching, Palme d’Or-winning moral dilemma pits preaching conservative Christian parents against a holier-than-thou liberal system.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Journey

A Place to Heal

Cédric Kahn’s watchful drama deftly captures life within an adolescent psychiatric unit, from the carers’ work to the kids’ trauma, friendships and lust for life.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Cédric Kahn

Screenwriters Cédric Kahn, Kahina Le Querrec

With Zoé Monpart, Malou Khebizi, Kenji Peyran

France 2026. 105min

Courtesy of Charades

Language French With English subtitles

Introduction

When 17-year-old Lucia is brought to the ward, she already knows everyone. It’s not her first time there, but the arrival of a mysterious young man threatens the fragile equilibrium of the unit. Combining documentary-style observations with a lyrical third act, alongside moving performances from its mostly non-professional young cast, A Place to Heal pays homage to those precious places that offer space to heal.

Laure Bonville

Content advice

Contains scenes of sex.

Contains themes of domestic violence or abuse, self harm, and suicide.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Lemonade

Barry Keoghan plays a social worker trying to make up for the past in this heartfelt coming-of-age Irish drama about second chances.

FLORID

In this striking British feature debut, a young man living in supported accommodation tries to juggle his musical aspirations and mental health issues.

La Dérive

The debut of French New Wave filmmaker Paula Delsol fell into oblivion, but her essential contribution to cinema is now ready for rediscovery.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Official Competition

My Notes on Mars

In Lili Horvát’s beguiling third feature, the sudden return of Sam’s missing wife, who has no memory of anything except her scientific research, gives their relationship another chance.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Lili Horvát

With Mackenzie Davis, Rupert Friend, Atanáz Babinchak

Hungary-Austria 2026. 108min

Courtesy of Paradise City Sales

Languages English, Hungarian With English subtitles

Introduction

A talented scientist goes missing while hiking with her husband. Weeks later, she reappears at the family home, but is not herself; all memories, save for those of her recent research on Mars, have mysteriously disappeared. This suspenseful domestic drama follows the couple as they navigate a second chance at life together, while questioning how much we can really know those we love.

Chloé Trayner

With thanks to Liszt Institute London.

Content advice

Contains scenes of nudity and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

La Gradiva

Youth shines dangerously bright in this luminous and captivating drama of high-school kids on a trip to study the ruins of Pompeii.

The Liberation

In Guy Nattiv’s tense, probing film, two young women attempt to extract their mother from a cult, but find themselves susceptible to its mysterious leader.

La Dérive

The debut of French New Wave filmmaker Paula Delsol fell into oblivion, but her essential contribution to cinema is now ready for rediscovery.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Shorts

I See Myself

From silent protests and secret ponderings to vocal uprisings and drastic acts, watch people endeavour to carve a bigger space for themselves in a world that’s trying to box them in.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Total running time 116min

Programmed by Sky Lewis, Victoria Millington

Content advice This short film programme contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, nudity, sex, racist attitudes and language, and themes of domestic violence or abuse.

The Animals

Director-screenwriter Calvin Demba

UK 2026. 18min

After another man is hailed as a hero, an insecure boyfriend becomes determined to prove that he, too, can protect the woman he loves.

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury.

Hindsight

Director Remi R.M. Moses

Screenwriter Benjamin Sarpong-Broni

UK 2026. 11min

Jamal’s first car is a gateway to adventures with his friends, but life soon takes them in different directions.

Content advice

Contains racist attitudes and language.

Free Eliza (notes on an anatomical imperfection)

Director-screenwriter Alexandra Matheou

Cyprus-Greece-France 2026. 20min

In a world obsessed with toxic positivity, Eliza must decide whether to change herself or resist fitting in.

Content advice

Contains scenes of nudity.

In Dreaming

Director-screenwriter Kristina Pringle

UK 2026. 7min

Ryan is destined to dance, but has to put his passion aside to fulfil his duties at his family’s nail salon.

Paper Plane

Director-screenwriter Saoirse Ronan

UK-Ireland

When a defiant girl stages a silent protest, an exchange of paper planes forces her mother to make a choice.

Content advice

Contains themes of domestic violence or abuse.

Last Minute

Director-screenwriter Sam Brain

UK 2026. 5min

As Mike gets ready to leave his life in London behind, his friend tries to convince him to stay.

Treasure Island

Watch for free on BFI Player until 25 October

Director-screenwriter Miryam Charles

Canada 2026. 18min

Summer 1993. Marthe convinces her brother to run away from home. Joined by their cousins, they debate what their future might hold.

Bermuda Riots are Different

Directors Alyson Thompson, Matt Mead

UK-Bermuda 2026. 6min

The picture-postcard image of Bermuda is shattered when archival and contemporary footage is interwoven with the unfiltered voices of the island’s people.

Content advice

Contains racist attitudes and language.

Aman

Watch for free on BFI Player until 25 October

Director Rahul Roye

Screenwriters Rahul Roye, Elle León Nostas

India-UK-USA-France 2026. 16min

On the eve of his gender-affirming surgery, a trans man’s journey takes an unexpected turn.

Content advice

Contains scenes of sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

As the Years Roll By

In reflecting on the past or embracing unexpected futures, time flows through people’s connection with others and the earth, in these shorts on life in the later years.

Altered States

Fractured memories and uncertain fates are examined in shorts featuring our unshakeable resolve.

Call Your Bluff

Whether it’s cutting your own hair, winning the lottery, looking for love or livening up a dull day at work, these uk shorts will cover all your comedy needs.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Debate

Amazomania

This reframing of ‘adventure journalist’ Erling Söderström’s 1996 Amazonian expedition to the isolated Korubo people is an unflinching critique of the ethics of first-contact filmmaking.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Nathan Grossman

Screenwriters Jordana Berg, Olof Berglind

Sweden-Denmark-France 2026. 93min

Courtesy of Autlook Filmsales

Languages Portuguese, French, English, Swedish, Korubo With English subtitles

Introduction

Digging into the Swedish journalist’s unreleased archives, documentarian Nathan Grossman flips a ‘White Saviour’ narrative on its head by juxtaposing extraordinary but deeply uncomfortable original footage with an alarming 2023 reunion, in which the Korubo finally get to speak for themselves. Amazomania is a fierce deconstruction of the camera’s gaze and a reckoning on who really owns Indigenous stories.

Sarah Lutton

With thanks to Embassy of Sweden.

Content advice

Contains scenes of animal slaughter.

Contains racist attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Rebellion

Revolution is the beat that drums through this electrifying story about the landmark case against the Bradford 12.

Tropical Fractals

Leonardo Pirondi’s timely reflection on ecological collapse imagines a future in which a biodome spaceship preserves the last traces of life on Earth.

Concrete Land

Asmahan Bkerat’s feature directorial debut is an intimate, multi-generational portrait of a mixed-raced family fighting displacement and hostility in Jordan.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Debate

Panelstory, or How a Housing Development is Born

Panelstory aneb Jak se rodí sídliště

A single day in a colossal unfinished housing estate on the fringes of Prague becomes a corrosive social satire in the hands of acclaimed filmmaker Věra Chytilová.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Věra Chytilová

Screenwriters Eva Kačírková, Věra Chytilová

With Lukáš Bech, Antonín Vaňha, Eva Kačírková

Czechoslovakia 1979. 100min

Courtesy of Národní filmový archiv, Prague

Language Czech With English subtitles

Introduction

A tragicomic gallery of characters composes this satirical fresco of a hellish housing estate. In this dysfunctional, endless chaos, people try to get on with their lives amongst the rubble and the mud of this new socialist nightmare. After being blacklisted for years, Věra Chytilová returns to her radical style with a film that still resonates in a society of individuals living in crowded isolation.

Giulia Saccogna

Digitisation carried out in UPP and Soundquare by the KVIFF in collaboration with Národní filmový archiv, Prague and the Czech Audiovisual Fund, funded by Milada Kučerová and Eduard Kučera.

Content advice

Contains racist attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

La Dérive

The debut of French New Wave filmmaker Paula Delsol fell into oblivion, but her essential contribution to cinema is now ready for rediscovery.

Gone to Earth

Long overshadowed within Powell and Pressburger’s canon, this major new restoration reveals the visual splendour and dramatic intensity of one of their most misunderstood films.

Pakeezah

One of the last great classical musicals of Indian cinema, the visually opulent and emotionally tragic Pakeezah is a byzantine story of star-crossed lovers.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Dare

Let Them Be Seen

Nolitha Refilwe Mkulisi’s debut feature – a tender love letter to Tapoleng, her hometown in South Africa – offers an intimate evocation of a community in transition.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Nolitha Refilwe Mkulisi

South Africa-Germany 2026. 75min

Courtesy of Brown Flamingo Productions

Languages Xhosa, Sesotho, English With English subtitles

Introduction

Once centred around Christianity, with the church serving as a sanctuary during apartheid, Tapoleng now finds itself negotiating shifting beliefs and identities. Blending interviews, improvised performance and observational footage, Mkulisi’s generous hybrid cinematic form embraces the rich textures of everyday life, creating a collaborative space in which her subjects represent and reimagine themselves on their own terms.

Hyun Jin Cho

Content advice

Contains racist attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

I Plant My Hand in the Garden

Playing versions of themselves as the central protagonists, Hoda Taheri and Boris Hadžija make a daring debut: a witty, irreverent and politically astute portrait of lives shaped by the search for belonging.

Variations on a Theme

The Tiger Award winner at this year’s Rotterdam Film Festival is a gentle and enchanting portrait of an octogenarian goat herder in South Africa’s Kamiesberge.

Ba’s Book

Ashley Duong crafts a heartfelt hybrid film in response to her father’s memoir, which recounts his experiences of the Vietnam War and Iranian Revolution.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Debate

A Good Little Soldier

Un Bon Petit Soldat

Stéphane Brizé’s taut exploration of the dynamics of power in the modern workplace features Alba Rohrwacher and Vincent Lindon at the top of their game.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Stéphane Brizé

Screenwriters Stéphane Brizé, Coralie Amédéo, Olivier Gorce

With Alba Rohrwacher, Vincent Lindon

France 2026. 101min

Courtesy of Gaumont

Language French With English subtitles

Introduction

Carla is the new head of HR in a large insurance company. Beneath the veneer of positive and inclusive management exists an insidious and crushing reality that will catch her off guard. Executed with chilling precision within enclosed, clinical spaces and propelled by an unnerving jazz score, A Good Little Soldier captivates and unsettles in equal measure.

Laure Bonville

Content advice

Contains ableist attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Ink

Danny Boyle brings a seismic moment in Rupert Murdoch’s Fleet Street career blazingly to life, employing the breathtaking style of a story torn from the headlines.

Fjord

This searching, Palme d’Or-winning moral dilemma pits preaching conservative Christian parents against a holier-than-thou liberal system.

Heysel 85

This is a gripping and sobering dramatic reconstruction of the tragedy that unfolded during the 1985 European Cup final between Liverpool and Juventus at the Brussels stadium.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Journey

Perfect Road

By turns exhilarating and intimate, this documentary portrait charts nomadic cyclist Max Schnell’s attempt to complete an extreme journey through some of Europe’s highest mountain passes.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Directors Adam Bonke, Christian Bonke

With Max Schnell, Nina Ridder

Denmark 2026. 91min

Courtesy of Dogwoof

Languages English, German With some English subtitles

Introduction

Max has been living on his bike for the last decade, pursuing what he sees as the most perfect form of freedom. While he undertakes his most gruelling challenge to date, his relationship with his partner, Nina, makes him question his life priorities. Adam and Christian Bonke enjoyed extensive access to craft a nuanced character study that unfolds against the backdrop of breathtaking mountain vistas.

Laure Bonville

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

The Match

Few sporting contests loom as large in the public imagination as the dramatic 1986 World Cup Quarter Final between England and Argentina, as this documentary details.

The Story of Documentary Film (The 1990s)

This fascinating chapter from Mark Cousins’ epic essay on the history of documentary chronicles a decade of formal reinvention and mainstream success.

Carl Sagan: We Are Made of Star Stuff

This awe-inspiring documentary is a detailed and thought-provoking portrait of the astronomer and astrophysicist behind Cosmos and Contact.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Debate

I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning

In Clio Barnard’s poignant drama, five childhood friends from Birmingham find their lifelong bonds tested as adulthood brings fractured relationships, unfulfilled dreams and long-buried secrets to light.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Clio Barnard

Screenwriter Enda Walsh

With Anthony Boyle, Daryl McCormack, Jay Lycurgo, Lola Petticrew, Joe Cole

UK 2026. 110min

Courtesy of Curzon Film

Language English

In association with

Access information

Friday 16 October 20:40

Audio description

Sunday 18 October 11:30

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Sunday 18 October 12:00

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Adapted from Kieran Goddard’s novel, this intoxicating yet compassionate film by the director of The Selfish Giant and Ali & Ava is propelled by a superb ensemble cast and the euphoric pulse of club music. As moments of youthful joy gradually give way to disillusionment, the film offers a piercing portrait of contemporary Britain, exposing exploitative social structures and widening inequality as forces that have deeply marked its characters’ lives.

Hyun Jin Cho

Content advice

Contains flashing images.

Contains scenes of domestic violence or abuse, drug use, graphic violence or injury, harm towards children, sex, and suicide.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Lemonade

Barry Keoghan plays a social worker trying to make up for the past in this heartfelt coming-of-age Irish drama about second chances.

Tender Loving Care

In a world that feels increasingly untethered from human connection, the incomparable Mike Leigh returns with a thought-provoking and compassionate view of urban life.

Club Kid

A jaded New York club promoter finds his messy lifestyle upended by the discovery that he has a son, in Jordan Firstman’s hilarious feature directorial debut.

content.article_text:
Films and events

Dare

Atlantic Rhapsody

Da Xi Yang

A young man embarks on a surreal quest to find his long-lost father in a remarkable feature debut that spans 20 years of recent Chinese history.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Zhong Kaifeng

Screenwriters Zhong Kaifeng, Wu Linfeng

With Yin Fang, Wang Yitong, Li Xueqin

China 2026. 101min

Courtesy of Rediance

Languages Mandarin Chinese, Japanese With English subtitles

Introduction

Opening with the unfortunate fate of a shark, which haunts the main character in unique ways, oceans – both physically and metaphorically – play an outsized role in this absurdist father-son drama. Zhong Kaifeng’s ambitious, award-winning film sees its complex sound design play a heightened role, as time and space collapse and blur.

Sergio Fant

Content advice

Contains scenes of animal slaughter and graphic violence or injury.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Hearing

Known for his precise and enigmatic filmmaking, here Lê Bảo crafts a meditative anti-love story revealing fragile connections between humans, sounds and unseen worlds.

Moonglow

The queen of sensual cinema returns with a 1970s Manila-set neo-noir about a police officer-turned-criminal under investigation by her former lover.

French Girls

Effortlessly moving from one moment to the next, Hyun Lee’s fashionably hip and charming micro-budget debut heralds an exciting directorial talent.
